body.text: Full notes

items: This briefing is for your eyes only, agent.
We're back! Another month, another update. Let's talk about everything coming your way. A new quest, new activities, Earth Magic and... Penguins?
Earth Magic
Finally - the fourth element has arrived. Earth Magic joins Air, Fire and Water, and brings a new, earthy flavour to Magic.
At level 14 Magic, you'll be able to equip Earth Runes for Staves and Wands. Earth attacks deal Blunt Damage, staggering enemies and interrupting attacks.

Earth Magic specialises in AOE Damage, launching waves of earth at the target. The final hit of the Staff Combo hits the area around the target too, catching nearby enemies. The Staff's Special Attack creates an earthquake, with multiple aftershocks. Charge it to increase the affected area. Once cast, you can leave it to do its thing while you reposition, to make terrain difficult for your foes.

There's also a defensive benefit to this - Armour of the Earth. Earth Magic hits build a defensive buff on you, reducing your damage taken. You can build up to 3 stacks, and they're consumed on your next incoming hit. You'll consume the stacks, and take less damage on that hit. Landing more hits keeps the stacks coming - so stay in the fight, push forward and maintain the stacks to reduce your damage. And, yes - At 60 Attack, you can enchant your melee weapons with this too, to build Armour of the Earth on-hit with melee as well.
Penguin Hunting

Ashenfall has been infiltrated by the Killer Gentoo Penguins - KGP for short - and we have received reports that over 200 of them have appeared across the continent of Ashenfall. It's time to get hunting. Penguins spawn in batches - no more than 3 agents at a time, per region. These reset at regular intervals of 7 in-game days so as you progress through your adventures, you'll spot more dotted around! Hidden in plain sight, these can be found, spotted and interacted with.

Once they flee, you'll collect a token - evidence they were here - leaving you a Penguin Coin. This coin will be used at a new shop in Bramblemead, with a Full Penguin Armour Set, KGP Hat, a Penguin Cape, and decorations for your base including new tapestries from iconic RuneScape Art Community founding member, and legend of the Forums:
Prezleek.

We've also added an amulet that improves chances to catch Pristine Fish, and a ring that reduces stamina for reeling in fish to make it easier to reel in the big one! These are the first steps we're making to improve fishing based on your feedback!
We'll be adding more rewards to the shop in the future so there'll be more to come back for, too!
A Reel Downer - New Quest

Over in Umbral Sands, someone’s having a rather difficult fishing trip. Head to the Manafem Clan’s camp for our new quest, A Reel Downer. Their fisherman’s catch won’t stop crying, and the clan can’t stand the taste of miserable fish.You’ll need to help him find a way to cheer them up. Apparently, happy fish taste better.

Finish the quest to unlock the Fishing Rod Rack recipe, giving your collection a proper display at home. You’ll also unlock trophy recipes for the sad fish, so if you catch a pristine one, you can mount it on your wall.
Nothing brightens up a home quite like a miserable fish.
The Rug Pull
There’s a new trail to uncover in Umbral Sands.
Four brothers stole a valuable carpet and some treasure from an ancient vault. But when the loot disappeared, greed and suspicion tore them apart.
None of the brothers survived, but they left behind their final journal entries, each telling their side of the story....
Find them scattered around the desert, piece together the clues and use the landmarks around you to work out where you need to dig.
Follow the trail to unlock plans for two new rugs for your base!
Letter Deliveries
If you’ve completed Letters from the Dead in Fellhollow, Postie Pete has some new delivery routes for you, taking you into Dowdun Reach and Umbral Sands.
Buy the plans for a regional post box using that region’s currency, then build it at your base. Each post box gives you letters for its own region, so you can choose where to make your rounds.
Deliveries in Dowdun Reach reward you with
Infernal Fragments
, which you can spend at Postie Pete’s
Evil Emporium
Over in Umbral Sands, you’ll earn
Garou Chits
to spend with the region’s merchants. Riches - or, a wage for your work, await!
PTR (Public Test Realm)
One suggestion we've heard a lot from players across our community spaces is something to the effect of "We'd love a PTR to help get hands on early and catch things if we can!"
We think that's a great idea, and we're taking our first steps towards making this happen!

We'll start with a select group of PC players who will explore upcoming builds, put the new features through their paces and help us identify issues that we may otherwise miss. This also lets us learn what works and what doesn't to make the PTR experience even better, if we are going to build it into a regular part of developing Dragonwilds.
What we want to be very transparent about a few things, though:

Due to the long lead times required for Console submission, any PTR on Steam is the build that is being deployed to consoles on release date. That means some of the issues discovered in the PTR before release would be resolved in a later patch.

Participation would also involve you backing up your saves and switching between a PTR branch and the Live version of the game. We'll provide instructions when the time comes, but it is crucial that you protect your progress when venturing across that Wilderness wall into the new branch!

We're going to test this out with a smaller, selected group initially to explore the branch, with dedicated spaces in Discord and Reddit to collate feedback - and contain spoilers. Our commitment in the wake of the PTR is that we will absolutely own, report and discuss what you discovered, what we're able to address, and what needs work. Diving into the PTR shouldn't just end with "Thanks for the feedback!" - we want it to feel like you know what happens next.
Bug Fixes
Fixed an issue where door opening animations looked smooth for the host but not for clients on that world.
Fixed an issue where Spell Books/ Spell Wheels would show the incorrect spells for the page when opened after using a lodestone or opening an interface.
Ascending Masterwork Armour now correctly increases its stats.
When filling stacks in chests, the stacks will now no longer pull from the Quick Access Bar.
Streamlined the process of interacting with Processing Stations to reduce the number of inputs.
Fixed an issue where Player-built structures on Dedicated Servers would lose collision and you would clip through them in certain circumstances.
Getting 99 Agility will now correctly trigger the achievement on consoles.
Fix for users who lost the ability to use the item wheel after using spell wheel hotkeys a few times.
Fixed an issue where summoning Sworn Servant "Buddy" would continually apply a Stamina Regen debuff even after despawning or expiring.
Added a new UI interface to showcase the number of enemies/waves attacking when a Base Raid event takes place.
Fixed an issue where clients in a hosted world would grow two trees from each planted seed.
Fix for the issue where the Quick Select wheel could not switch weapons during longer animations.
Fix for users who had adjusted their system clocks on PC being prevented from accessing Crossplay.
Deployed a fix where creating a new character using a renamed character's previous name would delete the original character.
Fix for Crafting Recipes that require six different materials that caused the UI to overflow into the quantity section.
Fixed an issue where users could use a broken 1-handed weapon by equipping a shield.
Resolved an issue where opening/closing the map would cause your inventory to stay open.
Resolved an issue where the Enchanted Weapon ambience has been tapped down.
Fixed an issue where Trunk Totem XP was multiplied incorrectly when various Trunk Totems were too close to each other.
Fix for High-Epic Graphics Settings displaying an incorrect LOD for a mountain in Umbral Sands.
Fix for an error message showing when disconnecting from the internet while logging in to Online play.
Resolved an issue where adding an item to your inventory would cause the inventory items to sort.
Resolved an Audio issue where Hosts would hear other players' Magic Wand SFX as if they were right next to them.
Fixed an issue where you could drag unrelated items into the fuel/combustible slot in the Campfire. Stop that.
Fix for a crash due to an audio reverb issue.
Fixed an issue where building menu icons looked pixelated.
Fixed a UI issue which caused the Compost Bins to display the incorrect status on use.
Fixed an issue where Gilded Gyrhawk, Glory, Strength, Magic and Salve Amulets were not calculating durability loss correctly with use.
Known Issues
Armour of the Earth Hit Reacts are not triggering their bespoke SFX.
If a player receives the same location twice in a row for Postbox Letter Delivery, the player must leave the area and return to complete the delivery.
In the Dowdun Reach area, the Camera unexpectedly pulls into the player model in certain spots.
Clients may appear as a default character for a brief time when first loading into a large world. Give it a minute and you'll pop right in as your normal self.
After being opened and then closed, doors will be slightly offset.
Using a mount appearance consumable without either base mount unlocked, will incorrectly show 'Mounts Unlocked'.
Pressing Up on the D-Pasd in the "Advanced" tab of Custom World Settings navigates up 5 menu entries, rather than the intended 1. Down on the D-Pad works fine!
These two in particular have been on our radar and we're introducing more telemetry tracking with 1.0.2 to help us better log data on these to investigate further:
Stuttering during auto-save following 1.0.1 update
In some instances, only one client will be able to join an Xbox-hosted world.
And that’s JUST this month’s update! Next month, we’ll have…
Luminance
This December, Elves arrive in Ashenfall with the Luminance Update, bringing a new adventure, the musical magic of the Lyre and a new way to build and shape your journey across Ashenfall.

You'll be exploring a new outpost area that will emerge from the fog on the edges of Ashenfall, meet new characters and learn to pluck, strum or otherwise noodle on a Lyre to resonate with songstones to progress! A continent wide hunt for a sinister Bounty Hunter will net you valuable resources and a way to earn Harmonised Crystal Fragments - valuable currency if you're in the market for new Elven gear. (You are, by the way.)
Embrace the Elven fantasy with a new Prifddinas-inspired building kit, a range of new character customisation options and craftable Elven armour and Weapons!

And what's a RuneScape adventure without another skill to level? Prayer joins Dragonwilds this December! Call upon Saradomin to smite your foes, Guthix to keep you and your friends in the fight, or Zamorak to trade a little health for some serious extra damage. Just remember, the gods all have their own ideas about how you should survive Ashenfall.
All of this lays the foundations and weaves in the first threads of our most ambitious, exciting questline yet in the Blood Crystal Saga. There's still dragons involved, of course.
Alongside all of this, we're continuing to improve the core experience with quality-of-life changes across platforms and targeted visual improvements for Nintendo Switch 2.
For now, that’s all we’ve got - but we’ll be in touch again soon. Until next time, have fun out there, adventurers. Be good, and we’ll see you in Ashenfall!

pages.summary: 1 raid / movement line: Anima vents are a good addition to help alleviate some of the (very intense!) relative scarcity of runes from other sources.

body.text: Raid and movement lines
Anima vents are a good addition to help alleviate some of the (very intense!) relative scarcity of runes from other sources.
body.author: Jagex · 2026-03-31

body.text: Full notes

items: Hi Adventurers, we're so glad to see so many folks jumping into Dowdun Reach and falling afoul of Black Knights! In the interim, we're seeing a lot of conversations around Runecrafting changes we rolled out with this update.
What we're seeing is:
The essence to rune exchange rate feels
very punitive
, and it feels like it takes substantially longer to craft stacks of runes.
The Rune Altar Attunement system doesn't feel rewarding enough compared to Auto-Attuning runes - the lean-in active skilling method should be more rewarding, and we agree!
Anima vents are a good addition to help alleviate some of the (very intense!) relative scarcity of runes from other sources.
We hear you - and we're looking at our options in terms of how we can make changes that aren't just short-term bandages.

Mod Bitf0x, Mod Pointy, Mod Zombie and I have been chatting this afternoon about what sort of solutions we can bring forward to address the issues we're seeing. We'll be looking into the data that we see over the coming day(s) to get a better picture of what changes we can make. Our intent is to always make adjustments that aren't going to need course-correction for us in the long term. What's apparent is that we do need to make changes to alleviate some of the pain points here, while still making Runecrafting a meaningful action that feels more rewarding, increasing as you level up.
We'll be sharing more news on this throughout the week and beyond as we continue discussions, but we didn't want to sit on this any longer. We'll be in touch - until then, be good!

items: RuneScape: Dragonwilds is celebrating its launch with our biggest ever Creator-driven event: Wrath of the Dragons!
Tomorrow, on Saturday 19th September, at 9AM PDT/12PM EDT/5PM BST/6PM CET, 32 creators will step into Dragonwilds’ 1.0 release, and will be given just
6 hours
to prepare a fresh character to beat the first Dragon in Dragonwilds - Velgar.
[img src="][/img]

Whether you first slayed a big green dragon in 2001, or 2026, you know RuneScape, so you know this story. Heroes are called to become a Dragon Slayer. This time, four heroes are called, together, to slay a Dragon - but Kuldra won’t let that happen without a few twists.

The wild anima of Ashenfall means that every hour, the world will shift with a few custom modifiers to make our creators more powerful - or more vulnerable! They might find that their attacks suddenly hurt each other, or that their hunger might be fatal if left unchecked. Their magic may suddenly have no cooldowns, or their crafting stations may suddenly surge with power and process much faster! Whatever powers they’re going to be getting, expect there to be plenty of chaotic moments and a few surprises thrown in for good measure.

pages.title: How do you beat the 6:50 Scorned Wilderness world record? A route you can run with
pages.summary: How do you beat the 6:50 Scorned Wilderness record? Get the movement kit, learn the 1.0.1.2 route split by split, and fly the Sanctum. This series teaches every step.

body.text: ***The 6:50*** is ***TexasPete's*** **6:50.000** run of the Scorned Wilderness raid, the **number one time** on the speedrun.com Raid board (version 1.0.0.6+). You beat it by combining ***Nanobit's*** **1.0.1 route** with ***Dotxy's*** **1.0.1.2 flight** and playing the five splits at the **community-best pace**.
This series teaches every step, in the order you need it. It is **a route you can run with**.
Is the 6:50 beatable today?

**The 6:50 is beatable on today's patch.** ***TexasPete*** played the record on 14 October, *"prior to the windstep double jump and some other new routing strats"* ([6:50 description](https://youtu.be/6WEIHo7AUf0?t=0)). Since then ***Dotxy*** has found a way to **fly through Kuldra's Sanctum**, and ***FastTipsGaming*** has shown a Stronghold launch with no Thane kill. Built only from pieces that still work on 1.0.1.2, the frame-timed run path adds up to **6:52.80**, and the **target pace is 6:48.10**, with the extra seconds coming from the Sanctum flight, the heart safespot and the Keep.

***Nanobit*** gives the verdict on the current route: *"clearly can be done sub 7 judging by my sum of best, but needs very clean movement and strong zoops"* ([7:01 description](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0)).
What is the Scorned Wilderness raid speedrun?

***The Scorned Wilderness raid*** is the end-game raid of RuneScape: Dragonwilds *(a chain of floating islands that ends at Kuldra, the God-Eater)*. The speedrun.com **Raid** category times it from the loading screen to the escape:

"Timer starts the first frame the loading icon disappears going into the raid. Timer ends on the frame the screen goes black after the "Get out now!" timer ends after defeating Kuldra's Heart." ([speedrun.com rules](https://www.speedrun.com/Runescape_Dragonwilds))
The run has **five splits**, each ending at an extraction point:
Segment times are measured frame by frame from each video (±0.1 s), as explained in **[Where is the 6:50 won?](#/kb?p=post%3Ascorned-wilderness-world-record-data)**.
Where does the board stand?
The board was read on **3 November 2026** with **zero runs awaiting verification**. The bracket covers every patch from 1.0.0.6 onward, so a run on **1.0.1.2** ranks directly against the 6:50.
How is the series organised?
The six pillars follow **the order a runner meets each problem**. Start at Pillar 1 if you have never entered the raid. Start at Pillar 3 if you already run sub-10.

items: **[Get raid-ready](#/kb?p=post%3Awhat-do-you-need-to-speedrun-the-scorned-wilderness-raid)**: every level, spell, item, quest and setting, and how to get each one.
**[The route, split by split](#/kb?p=post%3Ascorned-wilderness-speedrun-route)**: the 1.0.1.2 route in play order, every skip credited to its finder.
**[Movement tech](#/kb?p=post%3Adragonwilds-movement-tech-explained)**: zoops, dive cancels, infinite double jumps and Surge dashes.
**[Practice and consistency](#/kb?p=post%3Ahow-to-practice-the-scorned-wilderness-speedrun)**: drills and reset habits that land every skip every attempt.
**[Data and the record](#/kb?p=post%3Ascorned-wilderness-world-record-data)**: frame-measured splits, the sum of best and the pace that beats 6:50.
**[Patch watch](#/kb?p=post%3Ascorned-wilderness-patch-history)**: what each patch changed, quoted from Jagex, and the rules that decide what counts.

body.text: Who found the tech?
The series stands on the community's discoveries, and every post credits the finder by name:

items: ***Dotxy***: the **dive cancel**, the **infinite double jump** and **Sanctum flight**.
***SectorTSWG*** via ***Sir_Rebral***: the **skip to Fragments of Ghornfell**.
***Sir_Rebral***: the **Garou Thane kill through the gate**.
***IINo1goodII*** and ***notmusty1***: the **hole in Cataclysm Keep**.
***SamFPlays***: the **Surge + Phase Dash combo** and the follow-along route.
***Zilko***, ***CrossRSDW*** and ***FastTipsGaming***: the **Kuldra fight skips**.
***wes7918*** (***ChiefWes***): the **rib clip** at Kuldra's checkpoint.
***Nanobit*** and ***TexasPete***: the **records**, the zoops and the run notes this series measures.

items: Learn the **movement kit first**; every skip on today's route is built from five primitives.
Run to the **split targets 1:22.70, 2:23.20, 3:15.70, 4:42.30 and 6:48.10**: level with the 6:50 through split 3, about 8 s ahead after the Keep.
Spend your practice hours in **the Sanctum**, the swing segment: bring Dotxy's 51.9 s flight down to the 49.0 s target.

pages.title: How do you cancel a Jump Attack in Dragonwilds?
pages.summary: How do you cancel a Jump Attack? Cast any targeted AoE spell during the plunge, then cancel the cast. Dotxy's dive cancel gives you full control instantly.

body.text: The **dive cancel** *(also called the jump-attack cancel, JAC or plunge cancel)* is ***Dotxy's*** technique for **ending the Jump Attack animation instantly**: you cast a targeted AoE spell during the plunge and cancel the cast. You land with **full control of your character** and zero ending lag.

***Dotxy*** posted it on **14 October 2026**, the day patch 1.0.1 added the Jump Attack. ***Nanobit*** used it in the 7:01 the same week: *"Thanks again to @Dotxygaming for the plunge-cancel tech, it's very fun."* ([7:01 description](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0))
What do you need for a dive cancel?

rows: The attack triggers *"above the max height of the double jump's arc from the ground"*; *"Windstep counts here"*
The cast that overrides the plunge
A weapon with a plunge animation

body.text: How do you do the dive cancel?

items: **Get airborne** with **Windstep** or a **double jump**.
**Jump Attack.** The plunge animation starts.
**Open the spell ring** (`Q`) and **select any targeted AoE spell** during the animation.
**Cancel the cast.** You have *"full movement over your character instantly"*.
**Move, jump or dash** straight away.

body.text: Watch ***Dotxy's*** [51-second demo](https://youtu.be/LGCddmk_TnM?t=0) **now** and copy the rhythm on flat ground first.
Why does it work?

**Since 1.0, casting and movement overlap by design.** Jagex: *"This means you can opt out of those pesky wind-ups or spells you've committed to mid-combat."* ([1.0 patch notes](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1843481262704158)) The dive cancel uses that window: **the spell cast overrides the plunge**, and the cancel overrides the spell.
**It works off both jumps.** ***Dotxy***: *"this works with both windstep and double jumping, any time you're in the jump attack animation you can cancel it"*.
Where does the route use it?

items: **Fragments**: ***Nanobit*** at [2:13](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=133): *"Can likely plunge cancel here … instead of waiting to fall, saving a second maybe."*
**Keep exit rocks**: [5:07](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=307) and [5:12](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=312), *"as well as using the cancel to dash onto the first rock that I jump from at 5:15."*
**Kuldra's Sanctum**: chained dive cancels become **flight**. See [What is the infinite double jump in Dragonwilds?](#/kb?p=post%3Ainfinite-double-jump-sanctum-flight)

body.text: Which weapon should you hold?

**Hold a weapon with a plunge animation.** ***Nanobit***: *"remember that DScim doesn't have a plunge animation, so you need something else equipped."* ([7:01 comment, 5:07](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=307))

**Patch 1.0.1.2 touched the Dragon Scimitar:** *"Fixed an issue where the Dragon Scimitar would not allow users to Jump Attack in certain circumstances."* ([1.0.1.2 patch notes](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1847286114035869)) **Test the Dragon Scimitar on 1.0.1.2** before routing it; the mace from your gear list is the reliable choice.
What this means when you run

items: **Bind a targeted AoE spell** to the spell ring before your first practice session.
**Equip the mace** for every section where you plunge cancel.
**Add the cancels at 2:13, 5:07 and 5:12** once the dive cancel lands every time on flat ground.

***Dotxy***: "Note: this works with both windstep and double jumping" ([Dive Cancel](https://youtu.be/LGCddmk_TnM?t=0))

pages.title: How do you fly through Kuldra's Sanctum and skip the fight?
pages.summary: How do you get through Kuldra's Sanctum on 1.0.1.2? Fly with Dotxy's chained jump-attack cancels, take the fight skip, and clip through at the ribs. The record's biggest open save.

body.text: **Sanctum flight** is ***Dotxy's*** **1.0.1.2** way through **Kuldra's Sanctum**: a loop of **jump attacks**, each one cancelled by a **targeted AoE spell** and followed by a fresh **jump**, that keeps you in the air as long as you repeat it. It replaces the **Windstep up the blocks** that 1.0.1.2 closed, and it carries you to the **fight skip** and the **rib clip**.

Kuldra's Sanctum is the **fifth split**. ***Nanobit*** runs it in **1:56.15** and ***TexasPete*** in **1:59.38**, and **both runs predate the flight**. This is the **biggest open save** in the record.
What do you need?
See [Which spells and perks do raid skips use?](#/kb?p=post%3Aspells-and-perks-for-raid-skips) and [How do you do the infinite double jump?](#/kb?p=post%3Ainfinite-double-jump-sanctum-flight)
How do you fly through the Sanctum?
These are ***Dotxy's*** inputs, from his video description:

items: **Windstep.**
**Jump Attack.**
**`Q`** (opens the spell ring).
**Any targeted AoE spell.**
**`Esc`** (closes the spell ring).
**Jump.**
**Repeat steps 2 to 6** as long as you need height.

body.text: **Faster inputs gain height.** ***Dotxy***: *"If you're faster than I am you can gain height, not just hover"*. ***IINo1goodII*** adds that you can **dash and Phase Dash** inside the loop, and that he runs it **consistently on console**.
How do you skip the Kuldra fight?

**The Kuldra fight skip** takes you past the boss to the **Heart**. ***Zilko*** found the original, credited by ***Tiger with the Bars***; ***CrossRSDW*** rebuilt it after 1.0.0.6; ***SamFPlays*** teaches the 1.0.1 version; ***FastTipsGaming*** showed it working after the latest patch on **27 October** and again in a full run on **2 November**.

items: **Fly up** where the route used to Windstep up the blocks.
**Follow ***SamFPlays'*** fight-skip line** ([guide 9:18](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=558)).
**Plunge past the rocks.** ***IINo1goodII*** describes using *"the plunge mech to bypass the rocks on the fight itself since they are patched"*.
**Surge across the bridge**, as ***IINo1goodII*** does.

body.text: How do you do the rib clip?
**The rib clip** is a clip through the ground at **Kuldra's checkpoint**. ***Nanobit*** credits ***wes7918*** (***ChiefWes***) for it.

items: **Windjump into the exact spot** ***Nanobit*** shows at [5:33](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=333).
**Clip straight through** when your position is perfect: ***Nanobit*** measures **at least 3 s** saved over crouch-walking and a sword swing.
**Air dash twice** after it and keep your **Phase Dash** for the bridge.
**Stay to the RIGHT of the small white floating cube** on the bridge.
**Spend any Phase Dash you have left** at 6:20.

body.text: Does it work on 1.0.1.2?

**The flight works on 1.0.1.2.** ***Nanobit*** confirms the old route closed and the new one opened: the blocks *"no longer works as of 1.0.1.2/1.0.1.3. You can still get up to that area via just flying"*. The **fight skip** is confirmed after the patch by ***FastTipsGaming***. Test the rib clip three times on 1.0.1.2 before you route it.

**Ask the moderators before you use a macro.** ***Dotxy*** invites one for the flight loop, and the rules post covers what to check: [How do the speedrun.com raid rules work?](#/kb?p=post%3Aspeedrun-com-raid-rules-explained)

rows: Full raid and boss skip, 2 Nov (FastTipsGaming)
Original skip, credit Zilko (Tiger with the Bars)

body.text: How fast is the Sanctum flight?
**The Sanctum segment runs from the Sanctum door load to the Heart tunnel load** *(the two black loading frames either side of Kuldra's arena)*, so it holds the flight and the fight skip together.

rows: Drop into the void below the start platform

body.text: ***Dotxy's*** demo shows **50.6 s** from the first Sanctum frame to the tunnel load, plus about **1.3 s** of door load. The demo **lands and walks the walkway** from 0:21 to 0:38, so a direct flight line beats it.

**The target is 49.0 s**, about 3 s under the demo. **This is the swing segment of the record.** The flight costs about **17 s** against the patched blocks, and a runner on target pace gives back about 6 s of an 8 s lead here. Taking the flight from about 52 s to 49 s is what makes sub-6:50 realistic.
**This is a test step.** Fly the whole Sanctum without landing, time it from door load to tunnel load, and route it once you reach 49 s three times.
What this means when you run

items: **Drill the six-input flight loop** until you gain height every cycle.
**Hold a Phase Dash** through the rib clip for the bridge.
**Stay right of the white cube** on the bridge to Kuldra.

body.text: Read further

items: [How do you do the infinite double jump?](#/kb?p=post%3Ainfinite-double-jump-sanctum-flight)

([6:20](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=380))

pages.title: How do you practise the Scorned Wilderness speedrun?
pages.summary: How do you practise the Scorned Wilderness speedrun? Drill each skip in isolation, log every make and miss, reset with a full night's sleep, then link skips into full runs.

body.text: **Raid practice** is the loop that turns a skip you **landed once** into a skip you **land every attempt**: **drill one skip in isolation**, **log each make and miss**, **reset cleanly**, then **link the skips** into full runs against the record.
**Consistency decides this record.** ***Nanobit*** says of the Vines-to-Fragments zoop: *"At least half of my runs died here."* ([comment on the 7:01](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=105)).
Why does consistency decide the record?

**The record route is a chain of single-attempt skips.** ***TexasPete*** described it after his 7:40: *"If you have tried this, you know there is so many places that one small mistake will blow the run."* ([7:40, description](https://youtu.be/6N3NwYA5Zh0?t=0)).

**Clean execution is the gap to sub 7.** ***Nanobit*** on his 7:04: *"Overall just doing things more cleanly will produce a sub 7 considering my sum of best is 6:58."* ([7:04, description](https://youtu.be/KljLK0Z-9jY?t=0)).
What are the parts of a practice system?

rows: Repeating one skip on its own until it lands on demand.
Makes divided by attempts for one skip.
The skip with the lowest make rate; you drill it next.
Your best ever time for one split.
All your golds added together: your ceiling today.
Returning the raid and your character to a clean start state.

body.text: Which posts are in this pillar?

items: **[Which drills make every raid skip consistent?](#/kb?p=post%3Asegment-practice-drills)** The drill list by split, with the reference clip for each skip and how to log it.
**[How do you reset cleanly between attempts?](#/kb?p=post%3Areset-discipline-back-to-back-attempts)** The Air Thane respawn, the teleport floor hazard, rest and infusions.
**[Which inputs work on console for raid tech?](#/kb?p=post%3Aconsole-inputs-for-raid-tech)** PS5 spell-wheel layouts, PC number keys and the macro question.

body.text: What does a practice session look like?

items: **Set up** from the [pre-run checklist](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-setup-checklist), with a backup of your character file.
**Warm up the movement tech** on flat ground: dive cancel, then the flight loop.
**Drill your weakest skip** for a fixed block, logging every make and miss.
**Drill the Keep hole or the Sanctum flight**, whichever is weaker.
**Run full attempts**, split every one against **1:22.70 / 2:23.20 / 3:15.70 / 4:42.30 / 6:48.10**, and reset on the [reset thresholds](#/kb?p=post%3Areset-discipline-back-to-back-attempts).
**Review** where runs die and pick tomorrow's weakest skip.

body.text: Which build do you practise on?

**Learn on the safe learning route, then graduate to the record route.** The Raid Lab's **safe learning build** follows ***SamFPlays'*** 1.0.1 follow-along and is written *"for new runners learning the skips one at a time; consistent before fast"*. The **record build** pairs ***Nanobit's*** 7:01 route with ***Dotxy's*** Sanctum flight. Both list the same unlocks: Agility 44, Magic 11, Attack 25 and Magical Mending at Artisan 56 ([requirements](#/kb?p=post%3Awhat-do-you-need-to-speedrun-the-scorned-wilderness-raid)).
Where does the time spread come from?

**The Keep and the Sanctum hold most of the variation.** Across the six frame-measured reference runs (TexasPete 6:50 and 7:40, Nanobit 7:01, Nimblesk, ChiefWes, SamFPlays), the Raid Lab measured each split's share of the total variance:
**Spend your drill time where the spread is**: the Keep hole and the Sanctum flight.
How do you get more attempts per hour on PC?

**Force-close after a failed zoop.** A reply under ***Nanobit's*** 7:01: *"If you force close your game process after failing the zoop, you can reset raid progress to not-started to get more attempts without having to complete the entire raid every time. ... I recommend backing up your character json if you do this, just in-case."* ([reply on the 7:01](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=105)). **Back up your character file first**, then use it for Vines practice.
What this means when you run

items: **Log every attempt** on every skip so your weakest skip is a number.
**Drill before you run**, then run full attempts with the skips warm.
**Compare your sum of best** to 6:50 to see what clean execution is worth.

pages.title: How do you reset cleanly between raid attempts?
pages.summary: How do you reset cleanly between raid attempts? Sleep through a night so the air Garou Thane respawns, refill rest and infusions, and watch for the Commander teleport drop.

body.text: **Reset discipline** is the set of habits that put the **raid and your character back to a clean start** between attempts: the **air Garou Thane respawned**, **rest and hydration full**, **infusions stocked** and the **known hazards on repeat runs** handled.
**A clean reset protects the next attempt's splits.**
What resets between attempts?

rows: Respawn on reset or next run-through
Deaths no longer skip a respawn point

body.text: Why sleep between attempts?

**The air Garou Thane respawns slowly.** ***Nanobit***, on the day-one 1.0.1 route: *"Air Thane takes like 15 minutes to respawn, it's best to just sleep through a night after completing a run... otherwise he doesn't spawn in the next run and ruins your time."* ([8:32 run, description](https://youtu.be/vw_Mr5TGJAg?t=0)).

**The 1.0.1 notes cover the rest of the raid.** Jagex: *"Obstacles and Enemies now respawn in the Scorned Wildnerness Raid on reset/next run-through."* ([1.0.1 notes, Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1846651706673783)). **Sleep through a night**, then **confirm the Thane is standing** in the air room as your first Stronghold check.
**The same night refills rest.** A night's sleep is a **full refill** and grants **Fresh Start**; each death costs **15 rest** ([Rest, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Rest)).
What is the Commander teleport drop?

**The Commander teleport drop** is a **repeat-run hazard** at Kuldra: Commander Zilyana's teleport places you inside the ground and you fall. ***Bazilleos*** recorded it: *"Happens every time you repeat final boss. Commander teleports you to the next platform and in doing so you spawn in middle of the ground and fall down to the death"* ([Kuldra Boss new bug](https://youtu.be/JuuIF0BeGaE?t=0)). ***Vytautas Balnis*** filmed the same drop on 23 October ([clip](https://youtu.be/zl7R_N-vByw?t=0)).

**Plan around it.** **Reactive Recall** at Agility 70 turns a fatal fall into a teleport back to your marker ([Reactive Recall, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Reactive_Recall)), and **a fresh session** after a night's sleep is the cleanest state to test from.
How do you restock between attempts?

items: **Drink a fresh Fleet-footed Infusion** at the start: its Fleet Footed buff lasts **300 seconds**.
**Carry a second infusion** for the Stronghold. ***Nanobit***: *"Don't forget to re-use your fleet-footed infusion here, because I did."* ([7:01, 3:22](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=202)).
**Refill Strong Tea, runes and food**, then run the [pre-run checklist](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-setup-checklist).

body.text: When should you reset a run?

**Reset the moment a split falls behind its threshold.** The Raid Lab simulation searched for the reset points that give the most sub-6:50 runs per hour, assuming **45 seconds** from reset to the next timer start. For a runner at ***TexasPete's*** calibrated pace on his own line, the thresholds are:

columns: Reset if you are slower than

body.text: **Resetting doubles the rate of record-pace runs in the model.** With these thresholds the simulation finds **0.18 sub-6:50 runs per hour** (one every **5.6 hours**); finishing every attempt gives **0.08 per hour**. These are **modelled** numbers from a 20,000-run simulation, calibrated so the 6:50 is the best of about 177 attempts. **Use your own target splits** from the [run path](#/kb?p=post%3Ascorned-wilderness-world-record-data) as the reset line once you have a PB.
How do you reset fastest on PC?

**Force-close after a failed early skip.** A reply under ***Nanobit's*** 7:01: *"If you force close your game process after failing the zoop, you can reset raid progress to not-started to get more attempts without having to complete the entire raid every time. ... I recommend backing up your character json if you do this, just in-case."* ([reply on the 7:01](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=105)). **Back up your character file** before your first force-close.
What else drops you between attempts?

**Autosaves interrupt the flight loop.** ***FastTipsGaming***: *"If the game auto saves while you're trying to perform this trick, you're going down."* ([Infinite Jump, 0:57](https://youtu.be/U0_KPXu28qw?t=57)). **Log autosave drops separately** from skill misses so your make rate stays honest.

**After a full clear the raid resets to the start.** The wiki's quick guide: *"Once Kuldra has been slain, Commander Zilyana's ability to teleport you to locations other than Dragontail Vines will reset."* ([Quick guide, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Scorned_Wilderness/Quick_guide)).
What this means when you run

items: **Sleep through a night** after every completed attempt so the air Garou Thane is back.
**Check the Thane is standing** before you commit to the gate kill.
**Reset at the split** the moment you fall behind its threshold.

pages.title: How do you run Dragontail Vines in the Kuldra raid speedrun?
pages.summary: How do you run Dragontail Vines? Windstep to the first air anima, skip the soulscourge, skip the black dragon, and save every dash the 7:01 leaves on the table.

body.text: **Dragontail Vines** is the **first split** of the Scorned Wilderness raid, from the loading screen to the first **extraction point**. The 1.0.1.2 route clears it with **three skips** in a row: the **Windstep to the first air anima**, the **soulscourge skip** and the **black dragon skip**, ending on the jump-off point for the zoop to Fragments.
This is where ***TexasPete*** builds his lead. His Vines split is **1:21.52**, against ***Nanobit's*** **1:27.82**, so every dash you save here carries all the way to the cut to black.
What do you need?

rows: Launch to the first air anima
Four dashes to the first pillar

body.text: Every unlock is taught in [Which Agility levels do you need?](#/kb?p=post%3Aagility-unlocks-for-raid-speedruns) and [What gear do you bring?](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-gear-and-consumables).
How do you do the air anima Windstep?
**Crystallised Anima** is raid scenery you touch to **attune to an element** for 30 seconds. ***SamFPlays*** routes the **air charge early** so it opens the way ahead.

items: **Sprint from the first frame.** ***Nanobit*** walked for a moment here and names the cost: about 1.5 s.
**Windstep toward the first air anima pillar** and chain **four air dashes** on the way.
**Take three air dashes** toward the **second air anima pillar**.

body.text: ***zyneater*** adds a faster line in his guide description: a better route *"directly to the first air anima vent"*. Watch his [0 to 1 tips](https://youtu.be/1Q21XYSKJgo?t=239) and build that line into your practice.
How do you do the soulscourge skip?
***SamFPlays*** names it the **"Soulscourge skip (phase dash + food trick)"**. It carries you past the soulscourge area on a **Phase Dash** chain.

items: **Follow his line** from the [explained chapter](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=151).
**Spend the Phase Dash** where he does, and copy his food timing from the [original chapter](https://youtu.be/iu2SL4oyZFQ?t=40).
**I-frame Kuldra's first hit** *(i-frames: the invulnerable moment of a dash)* with a well-timed dash and a **tight line over the torch** into the first black dragon area, as ***Nanobit*** describes.

body.text: How do you do the black dragon skip?
The route runs **straight past the first black dragon** *(a power level 8 dragon that every route skips)*.

items: **Start the Earth Pillar early.** ***Nanobit*** measures about 1 s here.
**Take the clean line down** after the dragon to the **jump-off point**.
**Set up the zoop to Fragments**, covered in [How do you skip to Fragments of Ghornfell?](#/kb?p=post%3Askip-to-fragments-of-ghornfell)

body.text: Does it work on 1.0.1.2?

**All three skips work on 1.0.1.2.** ***CrossRSDW's*** older **Dragontail Vines skip** from patch 1.0.0.6 ([clip](https://youtu.be/lTG0EuXuqDs?t=48)) is a **research lead**: test it three times on 1.0.1.2 before you route it.
Load the ***SamFPlays*** clip **now**, then the ***Nanobit*** clip, and watch the two lines side by side.
How fast is each Vines skip?
**Each skip is timed checkpoint to checkpoint** in four runs (about ±0.3 s). The **target** is the pace that beats the record, built from the best valid piece plus ***Nanobit's*** time saves.

rows: ***TexasPete's*** line; hold sprint from frame one and take four air dashes
***Nanobit's*** line; three air dashes to the second pillar
***TexasPete's*** 7:40 line; Earth Pillar early, i-frame the knockback

body.text: **The split 1 target is 1:22.70.** The last piece of the split, from the black dragon to Fragments, is timed in [How do you skip to Fragments of Ghornfell?](#/kb?p=post%3Askip-to-fragments-of-ghornfell)
What this means when you run

items: **Count your dashes**: four to the first air anima pillar, three to the second.
**Dash through Kuldra's first hit** so the knockback costs you nothing.
**Arrive at the jump-off point with stamina** for the zoop to Fragments.

pages.title: How do you skip the Cataclysm Keep elemental puzzle?
pages.summary: How do you skip the Cataclysm Keep puzzle? Drop through the hole in the Keep that IINo1goodII and notmusty1 found, and solve Air, Water, Earth, Fire fast as your backup.

body.text: **The Cataclysm Keep skip** is a **hole in the Keep** that drops you **out of bounds** *(outside the playable map)* past the **elemental puzzle** *(four pressure pads stepped in the order Air, Water, Earth, Fire)*. ***IINo1goodII*** and ***notmusty1*** found it on patch 1.0.1, and ***Nanobit*** used it in his 7:01, thanking them for *"a lovely hole in Keep"*.
Cataclysm Keep is the **fourth split**, and it is where ***Nanobit*** wins: **1:27.80** against ***TexasPete's*** **1:36.30**.
Who found it?

**The credit chain runs through both finders.** ***Nanobit*** credits *"@notmusty1 via @IINo1goodII"*, and ***SamFPlays*** titles his chapter *"thank you @IINo1goodII and @notmusty1"*. Both posted their own videos of the skip on 16 October.
What do you need?

rows: Parkour and the jump into the hole
The rocks at the end of the Keep
Saved for Kuldra when the zoop is strong
Any weapon except the Dragon Scimitar

body.text: See [Which Agility levels do you need?](#/kb?p=post%3Aagility-unlocks-for-raid-speedruns) and [How do you cancel a jump attack?](#/kb?p=post%3Adive-cancel-jump-attack-cancel)
How do you do the parkour?
***SamFPlays*** calls this stretch **"Parkour section made easy"**. Follow his line from the [follow-along](https://youtu.be/WpvNjqVmpVM?t=320), then add the record details below.
How do you do the Keep hole?

items: **Jump into the out-of-bounds area** from ***Nanobit's*** reference point ([7:01, 4:38](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=278)).
**Land on the first rock** and keep moving; the extra jump onto the rock at 4:44 is optional.
**Plunge cancel** at 5:07 and 5:12 with a weapon that has a **plunge animation**. ***Nanobit*** reminds you the Dragon Scimitar has none.
**Use the cancel to dash onto the first rock**, then zoop.
**Save the Phase Dash for Kuldra** when the zoop is strong enough to need only one dash.

body.text: What is the backup when the hole fails?

**Solve the puzzle fast.** ***Sir_Rebral's*** advice from before the hole was found still holds: *"just solve the puzzle fast with smart pathing."* The pads go **Air, Water, Earth, Fire**, and ***SuperStooob's*** guide shows the solution ([14:33](https://youtu.be/7s3fgHwlRYA?t=873)).
Does it work on 1.0.1.2?

**The hole works after 1.0.1.2.** ***FastTipsGaming's*** full unedited run of **2 November** uses the same hole and push-through as ***Nanobit*** ([FastTipsGaming, 6:25](https://youtu.be/oK0_U_I40DY?t=385)), the first sighting after the patch. Land it three times in practice before a timed run, and keep the puzzle line ready as your backup.
How fast is the Keep hole?

**The Keep is timed in two pieces** (about ±0.3 s): the parkour from the split 3 banner to the Keep entry, past the last fire beam, and the run from the Keep entry to the **Sanctum door load**. The second piece includes the rib clip, taught in the [Sanctum post](#/kb?p=post%3Akuldras-sanctum-flight-and-fight-skip).

**Nanobit's 8.5 s lead in this split comes from the hole.** The 1.0.1 hole beats ***TexasPete's*** old Keep skip *(a blue rock climb, patched in 1.0.1)* by **8.6 s** door to door, and it beats the full elemental puzzle by **67.8 s**, the single biggest save in the route.

**The target is 73.5 s**: ***Nanobit's*** 75.2 s minus the plunge cancels at 5:07 and 5:12, the spare rock jump at 4:44 and an instant rib clip (at least 3 s). The **split 4 target is 4:42.30**, about 8 s ahead of the 6:50.

rows: IINo1goodII, the hole and the out-of-bounds path
SamFPlays, full puzzle (what the hole replaces)

body.text: What this means when you run

items: **Jump into the hole from Nanobit's 4:38 reference point.**
**Hold a weapon with a plunge animation** for the cancels at the end of the Keep.
**Practise the Air, Water, Earth, Fire puzzle** as your backup for a run where the hole fails.

pages.title: How do you skip the Garou Thane in the Shattered Stronghold?
pages.summary: How do you skip the Garou Thane? Test FastTipsGaming's no-kill launch over the island first, and keep Sir_Rebral's Thane kill through the gate as the proven fallback.

body.text: **The Garou Thane skip** is the route through **The Shattered Stronghold** that skips the Garou Thane area. The proven 1.0.1 version has you **kill the air-attuned Garou Thane through the closed gate** with a melee weapon, take his **air charge**, **windjump** *(a Windstep jump)* up to the **air door** and leave through a hole in the wall. ***Sir_Rebral*** found the gate kill, and ***SamFPlays*** credits him for it.
***SamFPlays*** calls this **"the HARDEST part of the raid"**. It is the **third split**, and it is ***TexasPete's*** biggest lead: **0:51.70** against ***Nanobit's*** **1:03.10**.

**A faster option arrived on 2 November.** ***FastTipsGaming*** skips the Thane kill entirely: he climbs the rocks left of the air door, Windsteps and glides over the island into the forest in about **51.9 s**. That ties ***TexasPete's*** patched climb, so this post teaches the **launch first** and ***Sir_Rebral's*** **Thane kill as the fallback**.
What do you need?

rows: Killing the Thane through the gate
The windjump to the air door
Drops from killing the air Thane

body.text: **A Garou Thane** is a Garou with a tower shield that blocks every attack until its stance breaks. **Crush** is its weakness, which makes a mace the right tool. See [What gear do you bring?](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-gear-and-consumables)
How do you do the no-kill launch?
**The no-kill launch** is ***FastTipsGaming's*** route from his full unedited run of 2 November, played after 1.0.1.2. It needs **no air charge** and **no mace swing**.

items: **Climb the rocks to the left of the air door** ([FastTipsGaming, 4:43](https://youtu.be/oK0_U_I40DY?t=283)).
**Windstep from the top** ([4:59](https://youtu.be/oK0_U_I40DY?t=299)).
**Glide over the floating island** into the forest ([5:00 to 5:19](https://youtu.be/oK0_U_I40DY?t=300)).
**Carry on into the parkour** toward Cataclysm Keep.

body.text: **This is a test step.** The 51.9 s comes from a tutorial-pace video with no on-screen timer (split point estimated, ±1.5 s). Land it three times on 1.0.1.2, then route it.
How do you do the Thane kill?
**The Thane kill is the fallback**, proven in the 7:01. These are ***Nanobit's*** day-one steps, matched to ***SamFPlays'*** chapter:

items: **Pass the water door** into the Stronghold.
**Kill the air-anima Garou Thane through the closed gate** with your mace. ***Nanobit*** notes the Thane *"likes to walk through the closed gate on his own"*.
**Air-charged, windjump from the tip of the rubble pile** up to the **air door**, and go through.
**Exit through the hole in the wall** above the **orb dispenser**.
**Re-drink your Fleet-footed Infusion** here. ***Nanobit*** names this exact moment.
**Zoop to the Keep** for distance. ***Nanobit***: a strong one needs **zero dashes** and places you at his 3:57 spot.

body.text: **Stop swinging the moment the Thane dies.** ***Sir_Rebral*** watched ***Nanobit's*** extra hit after the kill cost the 7:01.
How do you reset between attempts?

**The air Thane respawns slowly.** On 1.0.1 day one ***Nanobit*** timed it at about **15 minutes**, so he **sleeps through a night** after every run. Jagex's 1.0.1 notes say enemies now respawn on reset: check the Thane is standing before you start a timed attempt. The full reset routine is in [How do you reset between attempts?](#/kb?p=post%3Areset-discipline-back-to-back-attempts)
Does it work on 1.0.1.2?

**The segment runs from the split 2 portal to the split 3 banner in the forest** (about ±0.3 s for timed runs).

pages.title: How do you skip the poison area and the Abyssal Demon?
pages.summary: How do you skip the poison area and the Abyssal Demon? Skip the whole poison area with SamFPlays' line, then Surge and Phase Dash past the demon from Nanobit's exact spot.

body.text: **Fragments of Ghornfell** is the **second split** of the Scorned Wilderness raid, a Garou courtyard and a toxic castle that ends past the **Abyssal Demon** *(a teleporting demon mini-boss that follows you when you get far away)*. The 1.0.1.2 route clears it with **two skips**: the **poison area skip** and the **Surge and Phase Dash past the demon**.
***TexasPete*** runs it in **1:01.10** and ***Nanobit*** in **1:07.10**. ***TexasPete*** names this stretch in his commentary: *"Where all runs go to die."*
What do you need?

rows: Three long dodges past the demon
Extra air dashes after the Surge

body.text: See [Which spells and perks do raid skips use?](#/kb?p=post%3Aspells-and-perks-for-raid-skips) and [How do you combine Surge and Phase Dash?](#/kb?p=post%3Asurge-and-phase-dash-combo)
How do you skip the poison area?
***SamFPlays*** routes the **entire poison area** as a skip. His follow-along shows the line and his guide explains it.

items: **Land from the Fragments zoop** and follow ***SamFPlays'*** line from the [explained chapter](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=260).
**Plunge cancel** *(cancel the jump-attack animation with a targeted AoE spell)* where ***Nanobit*** marks it, instead of waiting to fall.
**Push into the hole with confidence.** ***Nanobit***: more confidence here *"will produce better (faster) results"*.
**Zoop hard at 2:32.** A strong zoop carries you to his 2:37 spot **with zero dashes**.

body.text: How do you get past the Abyssal Demon?
**The demon skip** is ***SamFPlays'*** **Surge then Phase Dash** in the air.

items: **Start the Surge from ***Nanobit's*** exact spot** ([7:01, 2:45](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=165)) so the demon stays in its area.
**Surge**, then **Phase Dash in the air** past the demon.
**Keep your line clear of the pillar** ahead, where a skeleton blocked ***Nanobit***.

body.text: ***notmusty1*** posted a **full Abyssal Demon skip** for 1.0.1 on 17 October ([video](https://youtu.be/rNDeEKsKGeA?t=0)). Compare it with the Surge line and test it three times on 1.0.1.2 before you route it.
Does it work on 1.0.1.2?
**Both skips work on 1.0.1.2.**
How fast is each piece of Fragments?
**Fragments splits into three timed pieces** (about ±0.3 s): the fortress run to the courtyard, the poison area and demon, and the golden path to the portal.
**TexasPete's 6.0 s lead comes from the two ends of the split.** He is 3.3 s faster to the fortress courtyard and 2.7 s faster on the golden path; the poison area and demon tie at **30.2 s**.

rows: ***TexasPete's*** 7:40 line; ***Nanobit's*** pond zoop to the gate saves about 2.5 s
30.2 s minus the harder push into the hole and the no-dash zoop
***TexasPete's*** 6:50; Surge from ***Nanobit's*** spot so the demon stays behind

body.text: **The split 2 target is 2:23.20.** The poison skip and demon line together save **14.0 s** against ***SamFPlays'*** follow-along route.
What this means when you run

items: **Plunge cancel at the drop** instead of waiting to fall.
**Start the Surge from Nanobit's 2:45 spot** so the demon stays behind you.
**Aim the 2:32 zoop for distance** so you keep both dashes for later.

pages.title: How do you skip to Fragments of Ghornfell?
pages.summary: How do you skip to Fragments of Ghornfell? Zoop off the rock at the end of Dragontail Vines and skip the whole necromancer area, the skip SectorTSWG found and Sir_Rebral spread.

body.text: **The skip to Fragments of Ghornfell** is a **zoop** *(a long launch off an edge)* that carries you from the end of Dragontail Vines straight into Fragments, **skipping the whole necromancer area**. ***SectorTSWG*** found it on patch 1.0.1, ***Sir_Rebral*** spread it, and ***Nanobit*** credits both in his 7:01.
It closes **split 1** and it comes in **two versions**: a **frame-tight zoop** the records use, and an **easier zoop into a respawn** that ***Nanobit*** ran on 1.0.1 day one.
Who found it?

***Sir_Rebral*** writes in his skip video that he learned it from ***SectorTSWG***, and ***Nanobit*** thanks *"@SectorTSWG via @Sir_Rebral for the new skip to Fragments"*. ***SectorTSWG's*** own run went up on the day 1.0.1 launched, with the note that he *"had to find a couple of work arounds"*.
What do you need?

rows: Dashes at the end of the split

body.text: See [Which Agility levels do you need?](#/kb?p=post%3Aagility-unlocks-for-raid-speedruns) and [What is a zoop?](#/kb?p=post%3Awhat-is-a-zoop)
How do you do the fast version?
**The fast version** is the one in the 7:01. ***Nanobit*** calls it *"relatively precise"* and says half his runs died here, so build it in practice first.

items: **Walk or run to the end of the rock** at the jump-off point.

**Zoop on the frame you start walking off the rock**, or the frame before. ***Nanobit*** explains the reason: the rock has *"an incredibly small slope after the flat part, before it drops off completely"*.
**Fly straight into Fragments** and continue.

body.text: **Walking gives you more time to react.** ***Nanobit*** found no distance difference between walking and running.
How do you do the easier version?
**The easier version** lands you in a **respawn** past the necromancer area. These are ***Nanobit's*** day-one steps, as written in the route:

items: **Zoop across to necro land.**
**Zoop off the rocks left of the bridge** toward the **top of the left pillar**. It needs height; use one or both dashes depending on the strength of the zoop.
**Respawn** (the zoop causes it) and continue.

body.text: Does it work on 1.0.1.2?
**Both versions work on 1.0.1.2**, and every 1.0.1 runner uses one of them. ***SamFPlays*** marks it **NEW** in his follow-along.
How fast is each version?
**The segment runs from leaving the black dragon arena to the split 1 banner**, timed in four runs (about ±0.3 s).

rows: Direct line off the dragon ledge
Direct line off the dragon ledge
Death at necro island, respawn at Fragments

body.text: **The target is 12.0 s**: ***TexasPete's*** 9.5 s line plus a 1.5 s margin. The **fallback** is ***Nanobit's*** zoop started about 1.5 s earlier, around **14.1 s**, which costs about 2 s against the target.
**The zoop beats the respawn by 24.5 s** from the dragon to the fortress courtyard (41.6 s against 66.1 s), because the respawn adds the *YOU DIED* screen and the wait.
Does TexasPete's direct line still work?
**This is a test step.** ***TexasPete*** leaves the black dragon ledge and goes **straight across to Fragments** in 9.5 s, a 1.0.0.6-era line that no 1.0.1 runner uses on video yet.

items: **Load his line** at [6:50, 1:19](https://youtu.be/6WEIHo7AUf0?t=79) and copy the take-off point.
**Try it three times on 1.0.1.2.**
**Route it when it lands**, and keep ***Nanobit's*** zoop as the fallback when it fails.

body.text: What this means when you run

items: **Learn the respawn version first**, then switch to the fast zoop once you land it every time in practice.
**Zoop on the last flat frame** of the rock, or the frame before.
**Test TexasPete's 9.5 s direct line** on 1.0.1.2 and keep the zoop as your fallback.

items: [What is a zoop?](#/kb?p=post%3Awhat-is-a-zoop)

***Sir_Rebral***: "The skip to Fragments of Ghornfell I saw in a video by @SectorTSWG" ([skips video, 0:53](https://youtu.be/r1nrG2NlW-g?t=53))
***SectorTSWG***: "Thankfully a couple still work including the boss skip, however I've had to find a couple of work arounds." ([1.0.1 run](https://youtu.be/s9cyeL2c-qg?t=0))

pages.title: How do you unlock the Scorned Wilderness raid?
pages.summary: How do you unlock the Scorned Wilderness raid? Complete Icthlarin's Little Helper, start Regicide, then enter from the north-western Fractured Plains in Ghornfell.

body.text: **The raid gate** is the quest requirement that opens the Scorned Wilderness: **complete Icthlarin's Little Helper and start Regicide**. With that done, the raid entrance in the **north-western Fractured Plains** of Ghornfell takes you to **Rasthin's Rest**, the hub where every run begins.
This post gets you from **quest log** to **first timer start**.
What do you need?

rows: The next main-story quest; start it.
The raid hub and the only place you can build.
The NPC who starts or resumes a run.
The extraction point at the end of each segment.

body.text: The wiki lists the gate as *"Complete Icthlarin's Little Helper; start Regicide"* and the entrance as *"North-western Fractured Plains, Ghornfell"* ([Scorned Wilderness, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Scorned_Wilderness)). speedrun.com tracks both quests as **Primary Quest** values on its Any% board, so they sit on the **main story line** ([speedrun.com](https://www.speedrun.com/Runescape_Dragonwilds)).
How do you get in?

items: **Finish Icthlarin's Little Helper** in the main quest line. Its final step is **defeating Fuzan** in the Umbral Sands ([Icthlarin's Little Helper, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Icthlarin's_Little_Helper)).
**Start Regicide** at the **Dragon Gate**: the wiki's start is *"Interact with the Dragon Gate north of the Fractured Plains."* ([Regicide, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Regicide)).
**Go through to the Scorned Wilderness** from the north-western Fractured Plains in Ghornfell.
**Arrive at Rasthin's Rest**, the hub.
**Set your bed spawn here** and **sleep** before your first attempt ([setup checklist](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-setup-checklist)).
**Talk to Commander Zilyana** to **start a new run**. The speedrun timer starts on the first frame the loading icon disappears.

body.text: How does Rasthin's Rest work?

**Rasthin's Rest** is the **safe hub** at the raid's edge. Jagex added it with 1.0 as *"a new area which players can build in, and the Raid area which does not permit building, because of the big dragon"* ([1.0 notes, Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1843481262704158)).

**Commander Zilyana** **starts or resumes runs**, and raid deaths place your **gravestone near her** ([Rasthin's Rest, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Rasthin%27s_Rest)). Since 1.0.0.5, *"Summon Shelter will be able to be used in the Scorned Wilderness hub"* ([1.0.0.5 notes](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1844751498218499)), so you **rest right at the start line**.
What are the five splits?
Each raid segment ends at a **Zilyana Teleporter**, the extraction point that saves your progress. The community split file uses the five segments:

items: **Dragontail Vines**
**Fragments of Ghornfell**
**The Shattered Stronghold**
**Cataclysm Keep**
**Kuldra's Sanctum**

body.text: **Splits 1 to 4** end on the **"Extraction point unlocked" banner**. **Split 5** ends on the **cut to black** after *"Get out now!"* ([speedrun.com Raid rules](https://www.speedrun.com/Runescape_Dragonwilds)).
What this means when you run

items: **Start Regicide** once, then the raid stays open for every attempt.
**Set your bed at Rasthin's Rest** so every respawn lands at the start line.
**Split on the extraction banner** for segments 1 to 4 and on the cut to black for segment 5.

pages.title: How does the Surge and Phase Dash combo work?
pages.summary: How does the Surge and Phase Dash combo work? Cast Surge for three long, stamina-free dodges, then chain Phase Dash in the air for extra distance.

body.text: The **Surge and Phase Dash combo** is ***SamFPlays'*** chain of **Surge dodges** *(three 8-metre dodges from one cast)* and **Phase Dash** *(extra air dashes while airborne)* that covers long horizontal gaps with almost no stamina. It carries you **past the Abyssal Demon** and across the **Sanctum approach**.
***SamFPlays*** opens his every-skip guide with it, in a chapter titled *"Phase Dash & Surge Combo"* ([guide, 0:00](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=0)).
What do you need for the combo?

rows: 3 dodges of 8 m, charges last 2 minutes, no stamina per dodge
Extra air dashes, up to 3 per cast

body.text: Values are from the Dragonwilds wiki pages cited in the Raid Lab mechanics wiki. Rune and level routes live in [Get Raid-Ready](#/kb?p=post%3Awhat-do-you-need-to-speedrun-the-scorned-wilderness-raid).
How do you do the combo?

items: **Cast Surge first.** Its three dodges each travel 8 metres, and they cost no stamina.
**Jump** off the edge.
**Chain Phase Dash in the air** for the extra distance.
**Spend the Surge charges** inside their 2-minute window.
**Bind both to number keys.** ***loopuleasa***: *"I spam Q+3 and Q+4 to enable surge and dash"*.

body.text: Watch the [Abyssal Demon skip in SamFPlays' run at 3:04](https://youtu.be/WpvNjqVmpVM?t=184) **now**, then his [explained version at 5:00](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=300).
Where does the route spend it?

items: **Abyssal Demon (Fragments).** ***Nanobit*** at [2:45](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=165): *"it's important to start surging from exactly where I do, so the demon doesn't chase you into the next area."* ***notmusty1*** posted a full demon skip: *"skip the Abyssal Demon completely! Fully working as today 17.10.2026"* ([video](https://youtu.be/rNDeEKsKGeA?t=0)).
**Keep exit.** [5:18](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=318): a strong zoop needs one dash, *"then you can save the phase dash for Kuldra."*

**Sanctum approach.** [5:52](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=352): *"You can probably air dash at least twice here (don't waste phase dash yet though)"*; [6:20](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=380): *"If you have any phase dashes left, just use them now."*

body.text: How should you budget the cooldowns?
**One cast per spell per segment.** Both spells sit on a **45-second cooldown**, so plan each cast like a resource.

***Nanobit*** weighs the Surge timing at Kuldra in his 7:04 notes: casting earlier and recasting at the top *"could still be faster, and save me a surge from the second side of Kuldra's bridge to her face (instead of jump/dashing), as well as one for the throat"* ([7:04 description](https://youtu.be/KljLK0Z-9jY?t=0)). **Test both timings** and keep the faster one.
What this means when you run

items: **Start the demon Surge** from Nanobit's exact spot at 2:45 every attempt.
**Hold your Phase Dash** through the Keep exit and spend it at Kuldra.
**Bind Surge and Phase Dash** to number keys before your next session.

pages.title: How fast can the Scorned Wilderness raid be run?
pages.summary: How fast can the Scorned Wilderness raid be run? 20,000 simulated runs per profile say the safe 1.0.1.2 route lands near 7:21; the record needs the unverified pieces.

body.text: A **route simulation** is a model that **plays the raid thousands of times** from measured segment times, skip success rates and failure costs, then reports how often a route beats a goal. For the Scorned Wilderness, the Raid Lab simulation ran **20,000 runs per profile** against the **6:50.00** goal and a **6:48.00** margin.

**Its headline is clear.** On the **safe 1.0.1.2 route**, even the ceiling profile has a median of **7:21.43**, and **zero of 20,000** runs beat 6:50. The record falls to the **fast, unverified pieces**: the TexasPete Fragments line, the FastTipsGaming Thane launch and a direct Sanctum flight.
What did the analysis measure, and what did it model?

rows: measured, contact sheets refined with 0.2 s strips
Thane launch −11.2 s, TexasPete Fragments line −6.1 s, flight +16.9 s vs the patched blocks
modelled: σ 0.0908, calibrated to ***Nanobit's*** PB 7:01.97 and sum of best 6:51 over 177 attempts
TexasPete's σ pooled from Nanobit, same attempt count assumed
modelled priors: elite runner 95% on working skips, 80% on new or unverified ones
partly measured (Keep puzzle +44.26 s, heart miss +6 s), partly assumed (failed fight skip +48 s)
modelled: 20,000 runs per profile, 45 s reset overhead

body.text: What did the simulation find?

rows: Best of both, as a typical run

body.text: **The 1.0.1.2 default route** is the safe line: Nanobit's vines zoop, the poison and demon skips, the Thane kill and air door, the Keep hole and Dotxy's flight. Its p10 for the ceiling profile, **7:10.17**, sits on the strict composite of **7:10.10**.

**The calibrated TexasPete profile** reads the 6:50 as the best of about 177 attempts, so his simulated median sits at 7:01.38. In the profile's own words: *"Medians slower than the PB splits because a PB is a best-of-N outlier."*
Where does the variance live?

Across the six measured runs, **Cataclysm Keep carries 29.47%** of the between-run variance and **Kuldra's Sanctum 26.36%**. Together the two back-half splits hold **55.83%** of it, which is where consistency practice pays most.
When should you reset?

For the calibrated TexasPete profile on the as-run route, the simulation's reset rule is: **reset when a split comes in later than** Vines 1:22.50, Fragments 2:24.75, Stronghold 3:16.00, Keep 4:52.75. That policy yields **0.1788 sub-6:50 runs per hour**, against **0.0812** with no resets: one record-pace run every 5.6 hours instead of every 12.3.
What does the 4:40 claim add?

**A second route shape.** ***IINo1goodII*** describes it: *"I launched myself skipping the 3rd checkpoint and some of the parkour area. Used the plunge mech to bypass the rocks on the fight itself since they are patched. Surge dashed the bridge."* ([comment](https://youtu.be/4hncfjhUvg8?t=0)) The run path reads his 45-second clip as a phone recording of a replay with the method hidden, so it stays outside the model until a timed run appears.
What this means when you run

items: **Route the unverified fast pieces** once they test clean, because the safe route tops out near 7:10.
**Spend practice on the Keep and the Sanctum**, which hold 56% of the run-to-run variance.
**Reset on the split thresholds** to double your record-pace runs per hour.

pages.title: What are Nanobit's 27 time saves in the 7:01?
pages.summary: What are Nanobit's 27 time saves in the 7:01? His pinned comment lists every lost second with a timestamp, worth about 29 seconds in total, led by the heart safespot and the rib clip.

body.text: **Nanobit's time saves** are the **27 timestamped notes** in his pinned comment on the 7:01, each one a place where his own run lost time: *"How to save time and some general tips"*. The Raid Lab run path puts an estimated cost on each note, and together they come to **about 29.0 seconds**, enough to take a 7:01 under the record.

**The timestamps are video time**, so every link opens on the exact moment. The **Est. s** column is the run path's estimate from frame timing; a 0.0 marks a note about consistency or reference points.
How are the saves grouped?

rows: Sprint, extra air dashes, earlier earth pillar, the Fragments zoop
Zoops, a plunge cancel, the demon Surge spot
OOB jump point, plunge cancels, dash economy
Rib clip, dashes, the cube, the safespot

body.text: Dragontail Vines

rows: "Tapped sprint in beginning but was already sprinting, so walked in beginning for about 1.5s before re-sprinting"
"Can do 4 air dash instead of 3 towards 1st air anima pillar"
"Can do 3 air dash instead of 2 towards 2nd air anima pillar"
"KB from Kuldra initial hit can be iframed with better timed dash + tighter line over torch into 1st BD"
"Earth Pillar can be started about 1s earlier"
"Falling down after 1st BD can take slightly better line to jump off point"
"Technically could start zoop to Fragments about 1.5s earlier but this zoop is hard, so safety."

body.text: Fragments of Ghornfell

rows: "Zoop from keep wall across pond can make it all the way to the gate with a good one, save maybe 2.5s"
"Can likely plunge cancel here … instead of waiting to fall, saving a second maybe."
"More confidence pushing into the hole will produce better (faster) results."
"With a good zoop here you can make it all the way to where I'm standing at 2:37, with no air/phase dash at all."
"it's important to start surging from exactly where I do, so the demon doesn't chase you into the next area."
"Don't hit this pillar lmao. Skele blocked my path here and I tried to adjust, poorly."

body.text: The Shattered Stronghold

rows: "Extra swing, not ideal. Don't forget to re-use your fleet-footed infusion here, because I did."
"This zoop can go far enough to require no dashes."
"This zoop can go far enough to place you around where I'm standing at 3:57. This saves A LOT of time if it works."

body.text: Cataclysm Keep

rows: "it's a nice point of reference of where to jump from, into the OOB."
"Extra jump up onto the rock here not needed, just missed the first one."
"You could probably plunge cancel here to save a small amount of time, but remember that DScim doesn't have a plunge animation, so you need something else equipped."
"Same here, as well as using the cancel to dash onto the first rock that I jump from at 5:15."
"Sometimes this zoop is strong enough to only need 1 dash, then you can save the phase dash for Kuldra."

body.text: Kuldra's Sanctum

rows: "you can clip straight through the ground at rib clip, without having to crouch walk up it and scimmy swing to clip out. This saves at least 3s."
"You can probably air dash at least twice here (don't waste phase dash yet though) and retain enough stamina to make the next jump here."
"With a strong enough zoop you don't need an air or phase dash."
"make sure you stay to the RIGHT of the small white floating cube you can see where the bridge would normally be, or you will bonk and fall."
"If you have any phase dashes left, just use them now."
"I slightly missed the melee safespot, I jump into it correctly at 6:53."

body.text: **Notes 23 to 26 carry 0.0** because they sit on the blocks route that 1.0.1.2 closed. ***Nanobit***: *"You can still get up to that area via just flying lmao."* Flight replaces that climb ([Sanctum flight](#/kb?p=post%3Ainfinite-double-jump-sanctum-flight)).
Which saves should you take first?

items: **The heart safespot (6.0 s)** and **the rib clip (3.0 s)**: the two largest, worth 9 seconds together.
**The Stronghold to Keep zoop (4.0 s)** and **the pond zoop (2.5 s)**: they need [zoop practice](#/kb?p=post%3Awhat-is-a-zoop).
**Free saves**: notes 1, 13, 14 and 18 cost only attention, 4.0 s in all.
**Tech saves**: notes 9, 19 and 20 need the [dive cancel](#/kb?p=post%3Adive-cancel-jump-attack-cancel).

body.text: What this means when you run

items: **Jump straight into the melee safespot** at the heart, the single largest save at 6 seconds.
**Sprint once** at the start and re-drink the Fleet-footed Infusion at the Stronghold.
**Add the fourth air dash** to the first air anima pillar this session.

pages.title: What are the speedrun.com Raid rules for the Scorned Wilderness?
pages.summary: What are the speedrun.com Raid rules? The timer runs from the first frame the loading icon disappears to the cut to black after Get out now!, with full video and audible game audio.

body.text: ***The speedrun.com Raid rules*** are the timing and video rules that decide **what counts as a Scorned Wilderness record**. The timer starts on **the first frame the loading icon disappears** going into the raid and stops on **the frame the screen goes black** after the "Get out now!" countdown.
Knowing the exact frames matters: **the escape after Kuldra's Heart is part of your time**, and a run without audible game audio stays off the board.
When does the timer start and stop?
The Raid category rules read, in full:

"Timer starts the first frame the loading icon disappears going into the raid. Timer ends on the frame the screen goes black after the "Get out now!" timer ends after defeating Kuldra's Heart." ([speedrun.com](https://www.speedrun.com/Runescape_Dragonwilds))

rows: First frame the loading icon disappears going into the raid
Start LiveSplit on that frame, or let a moderator retime from the video.
Community split file: the "Extraction point unlocked" banner
Split on the first banner frame of each area.
Frame the screen goes black after the "Get out now!" timer
Keep running through the escape; the cut to black is your final split.
Every frame of the escape counts.

body.text: ***TexasPete's*** **7:40** shows why the end frame matters: *"I accidently stopped the clock less than a second short. Total time was roughly 7.40.84"* ([7:40 description](https://youtu.be/6N3NwYA5Zh0?t=0)). The measured cut to black in that video sits at **460.62 s**.
What must the video show?
The game-wide rules apply to every Raid run:

"All submissions requires a full video of the run, including game audio. Game audio must be audible. The video link MUST embed on the run page (e.g. no URL shorteners or sketchy file sharing sites)" ([speedrun.com](https://www.speedrun.com/Runescape_Dragonwilds))
Two more lines from the same rules shape your recording setup:

items: **Persistent VODs**: "VODs should persist indefinitely (e.g. Highlight instead of Past Broadcast)".

**Visible HUD**: "Dynamic HUD elements should not be obscured or omitted (e.g. health, inventory, stamina)". Place your LiveSplit and webcam overlays **clear of the health, inventory and stamina bars**.

body.text: Every run is checked by the moderators, ***Archy*** and ***dotyoureyes***.
Which bracket does a 1.0.1.2 run go in?
The Raid board has **two version brackets**: **Pre 1.0.0.6** and **1.0.0.6+**. A run on **1.0.1.2** goes in **1.0.0.6+**, the same bracket as the 6:50 and the 7:01.
The Pre 1.0.0.6 bracket holds ***ShadowStalkerTM's*** **3:27** and ***heartlessedly's*** **3:57**, played on the extraction skip that 1.0.0.6 closed.
Are macros allowed for the flight loop?

***Dotxy*** suggests one for the flight: *"Feel free to set up a macro for easy infinite flight!"* ([Sanctum flight](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0)). The written Raid rules name **timing and video only**, and the game rules add a **good-faith clause**:
"Runs are expected to be performed in good faith and may be rejected based on mod discretion if performed otherwise." ([speedrun.com](https://www.speedrun.com/Runescape_Dragonwilds))

So **ask the moderators before you submit a macro run**, and practise the loop by hand in the meantime. Hand inputs are accepted under every reading of the rules. Learn them in **[What is the infinite double jump?](#/kb?p=post%3Ainfinite-double-jump-sanctum-flight)**.
{{update when the speedrun.com moderators (Archy, dotyoureyes) rule on macros for the flight loop: quote the ruling here and in the flight posts}}
What this means when you run

items: Split on the **first frame of the "Extraction point unlocked" banner** and run straight through the escape to the cut to black.
Record **full video with audible game audio**, export a permanent highlight, and keep the HUD clear.
Learn the flight loop **by hand** until the moderators rule on macros.
