pages.title: What are the windjump and the rib clip in the Kuldra raid?
pages.summary: What are the windjump and the rib clip? The windjump is a Windstep jump onto a ledge; the rib clip uses it to drop through the ground at Kuldra's checkpoint.

body.text: A **windjump** is a **jump made under Windstep** *(the Agility spell that raises jump height to 16 metres and slows your fall)*, used to reach a ledge, a rock or a doorway in one move. The **rib clip** is the windjump at **Kuldra's checkpoint** that drops you **through the ground** at her ribs, found by ***wes7918*** (***ChiefWes***).
**Every split uses a windjump.** The rib clip is the single largest movement save in Nanobit's Sanctum notes: *"This saves at least 3s."*
What do you need?

rows: Higher jump, slow fall, 7-second window after the cast, 3 s cooldown
A jump taken inside the Windstep window
Windstep costs zero runes while worn
A windjump at Kuldra's ribs that puts you through the ground
Windstep, a melee swing as backup

body.text: How do you windjump the Stronghold air door?
***Nanobit's*** day-one notes, with the Thane route credited to ***Sir_Rebral***:

items: **Kill the air-anima Garou Thane** through the closed gate with a melee weapon.
**Take the air charge** from the kill.
**Windjump up to the air door** *"from tip of rubble pile and go through"*.
**Exit** *"through hole in wall above orb dispenser"*.

body.text: Source: [8:32 description](https://youtu.be/vw_Mr5TGJAg?t=0). See it in SamFPlays' run at [3:40](https://youtu.be/WpvNjqVmpVM?t=220).
How do you do the rib clip?

items: **Windjump** from the rock before Kuldra's checkpoint.

**Hit into the ribs** at the exact position. ***Nanobit***: *"If you're incredibly lucky, or smart enough to figure out the exact position to jump from and hit into, you can clip straight through the ground at rib clip"*.
**Fallback:** crouch walk up the rib and swing to clip out, the slower version Nanobit replaces.
**Continue** to the Sanctum approach.

body.text: Watch [5:33 in the 7:01](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=333) **now**, and the swing at [5:38](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=338) that ***loopuleasa*** called *"CHEFS KISS"*.
Who found the rib clip?

**Credit goes to *wes7918*.** ***Nanobit*** lists the source in his 7:04 notes: *"@wes7918 (Rib Clip at Kuldra Checkpoint)"* ([7:04 description](https://youtu.be/KljLK0Z-9jY?t=0)). ***wes7918*** describes it himself: *"i was the one who found the strat to jump on the bone and punch up to get back out into the map"* ([7:01 comment](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0)).
Which windjumps changed with the patches?

**Patch 1.0.1 targeted Windstep:** *"Fixed several Windstep-related skips in the Scorned Wilderness Raid."* ([Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1846651706673783)) **1.0.1.2** removed TexasPete's rock landing; ***Keimbho***: *"the new update made the rock a phantom. Can't land on it anymore."* ([6:50 comment](https://youtu.be/6WEIHo7AUf0?t=0)) **Test the rib clip on 1.0.1.2** three times before you route it.
What this means when you run

items: **Windjump from the rubble tip** to the Stronghold air door every attempt.
**Practise the rib-clip position** until the clip lands without the crouch walk.
**Retest every windjump** after each patch before you route it.

pages.title: What did each patch do to the Scorned Wilderness speedrun route?
pages.summary: What did each patch do to the raid route? Six patches in five weeks closed the old skips, and patch 1.0.1 added the Jump Attack that powers today's flight.

body.text: ***Patch watch*** is the record of **what each Dragonwilds patch did to the Scorned Wilderness raid route**. Six patches in five weeks closed the early skips, and the same patches handed runners the **Jump Attack** that powers today's flight.
Every route post in this series links here, so you always know **which skips are live**.
Why does patch history decide the record?

***The 6:50*** and ***the 7:01*** were played on **different patches**. ***TexasPete's*** run sits on the pre-1.0.1 route, and ***Nanobit's*** sits on 1.0.1 / 1.0.1.1. The speedrun.com board ranks both in **one bracket, 1.0.0.6+**, so a run on **today's patch** competes directly with the 6:50.
The patch line tells you **which segments of each record you can still copy** and **where new tech buys the time back**.
What did each patch change?

rows: "Added the Scorned Wilderness region… Added new end-game boss, Kuldra, the God-Eater!"
Raid released. ***CrossRSDW*** shows the load-zone extraction skip; the sub-4 era begins.
"Dying in the Scorned Wilderness Raid will no longer skip a respawn point."
The notes list zero raid lines.
Extraction skip closed; speedrun.com splits the board into **Pre 1.0.0.6** and **1.0.0.6+**. ***CrossRSDW*** finds new Vines, jump-puzzle and Stronghold skips.
"Fixed several Windstep-related skips in the Scorned Wilderness Raid."
Keep out-of-bounds closed. **Jump Attack** added, which powers ***Dotxy's*** **dive cancel** the same day.
"Fixes for skips in the Scorned Wilderness Raid."
The Windstep climb up the blocks to Kuldra closes; ***Dotxy*** flies through the Sanctum the same day.

body.text: The newest patch has its own post: **[What did patch 1.0.1.2 change for raid speedruns?](#/kb?p=post%3Awhat-patch-1-0-1-2-changed-for-raid-speedruns)**. The rules that decide what counts are in **[What are the speedrun.com Raid rules?](#/kb?p=post%3Aspeedrun-com-raid-rules-explained)**.
What did patch 1.0.1 add?
**Patch 1.0.1 built today's route.** It closed old skips and, in the same notes, **introduced the Jump Attack**:

"above the max height of the double jump's arc from the ground, inputting an attack will plunge you downward to slam into unfortunate victims below. Damage scales with the weapon you have equipped, so make sure you're holding something hefty before you leap. And yes, Windstep counts here." ([1.0.1 notes](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1846651706673783))

***Dotxy*** posted the **dive cancel** that morning: *"instantly exit the jump attack animation and ending lag by casting a targeted AOE spell, cancel the cast to gain full movement over your character instantly"* ([Dive Cancel](https://youtu.be/LGCddmk_TnM?t=0)). Every 1.0.1.2 flight is built on that one paragraph of patch notes.
Patch 1.0.1 also changed **practice**: "Obstacles and Enemies now respawn in the Scorned Wildnerness Raid on reset/next run-through." Every attempt is now **a fresh instance**.
What comes next?

Jagex has posted **nothing newer than 1.0.1.2 on Steam** as of 3 November 2026, and has teased **1.0.2 for next month**. Runners expect flight to be the next target: *"I love the tech but unfortunately they will probably patch it out again"* ([comment on Dotxy's flight](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0)).
**The best window to beat 6:50 with flight is now.**
{{update when the next Dragonwilds patch (1.0.2 or a 1.0.1.x hotfix) posts on Steam: add its row, quote its raid lines and re-test every route skip}}
What this means when you run

items: Read the **patch number on the title screen** before every session and compare it with the newest row above.
Route only skips with **evidence on 1.0.1.2**; re-test the rest three times before you rely on them.
Treat every new patch as **a fresh opening**: 1.0.1 closed skips and opened flight on the same day.

pages.title: What did patch 1.0.1.2 change for raid speedruns?
pages.summary: What did patch 1.0.1.2 change for raid speedruns? It closed the Windstep climb to Kuldra and TexasPete's rock, and Dotxy's flight replaced both the same day.

body.text: ***Patch 1.0.1.2*** is the **23 October 2026** Dragonwilds hotfix whose raid line reads, in full, **"Additional fixes for Kuldra Skips."** It is the **current patch** for raid speedruns, and the patch every route post in this series is checked against.
Jagex lists **one raid line**, and the community mapped the rest by testing. This post collects **what they found**, with the source for each finding.
What closed in 1.0.1.2?

**1. The Windstep climb up the blocks to Kuldra.** ***Nanobit*** states it at the top of his 7:01 description: *"Windstepping up the blocks to Kuldra no longer works as of 1.0.1.2/1.0.1.3."* ([7:01 description](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0))

**2. TexasPete's rock near Kuldra.** Commenters on the 6:50 report it the same week: *"the new update made the rock a phantom. Can't land on it anymore."* ([comment on the 6:50](https://youtu.be/6WEIHo7AUf0?t=0))
Both closures sit in **the Sanctum**, the split where ***TexasPete*** spent **119.38 s** and ***Nanobit*** **116.15 s**. That is exactly where the new tech lands.
What replaced them?
**Flight.** ***Dotxy*** posted a Sanctum route **the same day** the patch shipped:
"Heyo, here's a new way to get through Kuldra's Sanctum quick in the Runescape Dragonwilds 1.0.1.2 hotfix!" ([Sanctum flight](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0))
The loop, in ***Dotxy's*** own steps:

items: Windstep
Jump Attack
`Q` (Spell Ring)
Any targeted AoE spell
`Esc` (closes the Spell Ring)
Jump

body.text: "Repeat steps 2-6 as needed!" Learn it in **[What is the infinite double jump?](#/kb?p=post%3Ainfinite-double-jump-sanctum-flight)** and route it in **[How do you fly through Kuldra's Sanctum?](#/kb?p=post%3Akuldras-sanctum-flight-and-fight-skip)**.
What still works on 1.0.1.2?

rows: ***FastTipsGaming*** shows it "after the latest 1.0.1 patch" on 27 Oct ([video](https://youtu.be/L-dTDXJyFq0?t=0)) and in a full unedited run on 2 Nov ([video](https://youtu.be/oK0_U_I40DY?t=0)).
***Dotxy***: "This works mostly everywhere, happy flying friends" ([video](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0)).
***IINo1goodII***: "I've been doing this consistently on console." ([comment](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0))
***FastTipsGaming's*** 2 Nov run takes the same hole and push-through as ***Nanobit***, 98.6 s door to door at tutorial pace ([Keep at 6:25](https://youtu.be/oK0_U_I40DY?t=385)).

***FastTipsGaming*** climbs the rocks left of the air door, Windsteps and glides into the forest: about 51.9 s from the portal, against 63.1 s for the Thane kill in the 7:01 ([launch at 4:41](https://youtu.be/oK0_U_I40DY?t=281)).
***FastTipsGaming's*** full unedited run on 2 Nov plays every split on the current build.

body.text: Is there a faster lead?
***IINo1goodII*** posted **"Kuldra skipped in 4 mins 40 seconds"** on 28 October, after 1.0.1.2:
"Sub 4 mins is possible. I'm confident someone could do it in around 3 minutes flat. Not showing full clip or methods used.. sorry guys." ([video](https://youtu.be/4hncfjhUvg8?t=0))

In a comment he outlines the method: *"I launched myself skipping the 3rd checkpoint and some of the parkour area. Used the plunge mech to bypass the rocks on the fight itself since they are patched. Surge dashed the bridge."*

The run sits **off speedrun.com** and its timing method is unstated, so treat it as **a direction to explore**: a launch past the third checkpoint, plunge past the rocks, Surge across the bridge. Ask in the **[RSDW Speedrunning Discord](https://discord.gg/aGZkuC5yK6)**, which ***Nanobit*** names as the hub.
What should you re-test today?

items: **The Stronghold launch.** Copy ***FastTipsGaming's*** climb left of the air door three times. It is the newest save on the route and ties ***TexasPete's*** patched climb (51.7 s). Keep ***Sir_Rebral's*** Thane kill as the fallback.

**Back-to-back attempts.** On repeat runs the Commander teleport can drop you through the floor. ***Bazilleos***: *"Happens every time you repeat final boss. Commander teleports you to the next platform and in doing so you spawn in middle of the ground and fall down to the death"* ([video](https://youtu.be/JuuIF0BeGaE?t=0)). Plan resets in **[How do you reset for back-to-back raid attempts?](#/kb?p=post%3Areset-discipline-back-to-back-attempts)**.

**Your patch number.** Confirm the title screen reads 1.0.1.2 before every session. **1.0.1.3** is referenced by ***Nanobit*** and by NRS NEO ([video](https://youtu.be/0HeTn4G7oVk?t=0)) with no Steam post, so it is likely a silent hotfix.

items: Route the **Sanctum with flight**; the block climb and the rock are closed on 1.0.1.2.
Keep the **Kuldra fight skip** in the route; it is confirmed twice after the patch.
Route the **Keep hole**; ***FastTipsGaming's*** 2 Nov run shows it working after the patch.

pages.title: What do you need to speedrun the Scorned Wilderness raid?
pages.summary: What do you need to speedrun the Scorned Wilderness raid? Agility 44, Surge, the Jump Attack perk, a targeted AoE spell, a Fleet-footed Infusion and the Regicide quest gate.

body.text: **Raid-ready** is the state where your character owns **every unlock the record route uses** before the timer starts: the **Agility movement kit**, three **spells**, one **combat perk**, a short list of **consumables** and the **quest gate** that opens the raid.
This pillar turns that list into **five short posts**. Each one names the requirement, the **level or cost**, and **how to get it**, with the source quoted.
Why do requirements come first?

**Every skip in the current route is built from unlocks.** The Fragments zoop uses **Air Dash**, the Abyssal Demon skip uses **Surge** and **Phase Dash**, and ***Dotxy's*** Sanctum flight uses **Windstep**, the **Jump Attack** and a **targeted AoE spell** on your ring.

The wiki states the rule for the whole kit: Agility *"unlocks the whole movement kit: Windstep, Double Jump, Air Dash, Phase Dash and Recall"* ([Agility, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Agility)). **Level the character first**, then learn the route.
What is on the requirement list?

rows: Icthlarin's Little Helper complete, Regicide started
Runecrafting 1 Air, 3 Astral, 15 Earth, 38 Nature, 50 Law (wiki)

body.text: Which posts are in this pillar?

items: **[How do you unlock the Scorned Wilderness raid?](#/kb?p=post%3Ahow-to-unlock-the-scorned-wilderness-raid)** The quest gate, the entrance and Rasthin's Rest.

**[Which spells and perks do raid skips use?](#/kb?p=post%3Aspells-and-perks-for-raid-skips)** Surge, Tempest Shield, Enfeeble, the Jump Attack and the AoE spell.
**[What gear and consumables should you bring?](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-gear-and-consumables)** ***SamFPlays'*** gear list with recipes.
**[What should you set up before every raid attempt?](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-setup-checklist)** Rest, hydration, respawn, keybinds and the split file.

body.text: Where does each unlock land on a fresh account?
The ***Raid Lab*** Hardcore 1 to Max route places every unlock in a phase, and the build sheets in the Raid Lab repo follow the same order:

rows: Windstep, Double Jump, Air runes (Rune Mysteries), Leggings of Lightness
Tempest Shield, Surge, Air Dash, Superheat (Artisan 20)
Recall, *Death From Above!* (Attack 25, placed between Attack 11 and 30)
Reactive Recall, Enfeeble, Icthlarin's Little Helper complete
Regicide started, Fleet-footed Infusion, Strong Tea

body.text: **Law runes are the one source conflict.** The wiki states *"Law runes can be crafted at a rune altar at level 50 Runecrafting or higher"* ([Law Rune, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Law_Rune)), while the Hardcore route lists Runecrafting 16. **Check it in-game**, and stock up from **Garou Packs**, which drop **5 to 10 Law runes** at a **10/100** rate ([Garou Pack, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Garou_Pack)).
Which build should you follow?
The Raid Lab publishes **four builds**, each with its stats, items, ring loadout, keybinds and pre-run state:

rows: Theory: ***Nanobit's*** 7:01 route plus ***Dotxy's*** flight; no posted run uses it yet
New runners, one skip at a time
***SamFPlays'*** 1.0.1 follow-along; re-test Vines to Keep on 1.0.1.2
Repo plan with Reactive Recall always on

body.text: **Start on the safe learning route**, then move to the record route once the zoops and the flight loop land on demand.
What this means when you run

items: **Reach Agility 44 and Magic 11** before your first timed attempt.
**Put Magical Mending on your ring** and unlock *Death From Above!* at Attack 25.
**Pack a Fleet-footed Infusion** every single run.

pages.title: What gear and consumables should you bring to a raid speedrun?
pages.summary: What gear should you bring to a Scorned Wilderness speedrun? A Fleet-footed Infusion, Strong Tea, your best mace, a 2H mage staff and your best mage armour.

body.text: **The raid speedrun loadout** is the short list of **items and drinks** the record route carries: a **Fleet-footed Infusion**, **Strong Tea**, your **best mace**, a **two-handed mage staff** and your **best mage armour**. ***SamFPlays*** published it with his skip guide, and every post-1.0.1 route uses it.
What goes in the backpack?

rows: Sprint costs **50% less stamina** for **300 s**; +40 hydration
**1 Clean Water + 1 Feathers** at a Stone or Cooking Range
**1 Ground Tea Leaves + 3 Clean Water** at a Cooking Range
Kills the air Garou Thane through the gate
**6 Coarse Animal Fur + 6 Rune Essence** at a Crafting Table

body.text: Recipes and effects come from the wiki pages cited below.
Why is the Fleet-footed Infusion mandatory?

**The Fleet-footed Infusion** grants the **Fleet Footed** perk: *sprinting costs 50% less stamina for 300 seconds* ([Fleet-footed infusion, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Fleet-footed_infusion)). ***SamFPlays*** puts it first: *"Fleet Foot Infusion: MUST BRING. Cuts sprinting stamina cost by 50%."* ([Every Skip Explained, 1:43](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=103)).

**300 seconds is shorter than a 6:50 run.** ***Nanobit*** re-drinks it in the Stronghold: *"Don't forget to re-use your fleet-footed infusion here, because I did."* ([7:01, 3:22](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=202)). **Carry two.**

**Infusions share one slot.** The wiki's Kuldra strategy page notes they do not stack with each other, so the Fleet-footed Infusion replaces a Pumpkin Spice Infusion ([Kuldra/Strategies, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Kuldra/Strategies)).
Why bring Strong Tea?

**Strong Tea** restores **20 Rest**, and inside the raid it is your **only rest source**: the wiki states *"Resting cannot be performed during combat or a raid"* ([Rest, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Rest)). ***SamFPlays*** rates it *"nice to have, restores +20 Rest"* ([1:43](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=103)).
Why a mace, a staff and mage armour?

**The mace** kills the **air Garou Thane through the closed gate** on ***Sir_Rebral's*** Stronghold route. The Garou Thane's weakness is **crush** ([Garou Thane, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Garou_Thane)), which a mace deals. ***SamFPlays***: *"Melee weapon: Best mace you have"*.

**The staff and armour** finish the run. ***SamFPlays***: *"Mage weapon: 2-handed mage staff for killing the heart at the end."* and *"Armour: best mage gear you have."* ([1:43](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=103)).
**Pick a jump-attack weapon** for the cancels. ***Nanobit*** notes the Dragon Scimitar *"doesn't have a plunge animation"* ([7:01, 5:07](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=307)).
Where do Leggings of Lightness come from?

**Leggings of Lightness** come from the **Suspiciously Light Tattered Boots** vestige in a chest **atop the Temple Woods windmill** ([Leggings of Lightness, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Leggings_of_Lightness)). Since 1.0, Jagex *"replaced it with an ability that makes Windstep cost zero runes to cast while the Leggings are equipped"* ([1.0 notes, Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1843481262704158)). The trade is **zero leg armour**.
Which tier of gear do you need?

**Power level 7 is the floor.** The wiki's Regicide page recommends *"Power level 7 or better armour and weapons"* ([Regicide, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Regicide)). On the Raid Lab Hardcore route that tier comes from **Umbral Sands** (Phase 5), where the Nightmare Crucibles' Ascension Cores lift your weapon from power level 6 to 7.

rows: Best mace, plus a shield for the Thane

body.text: **The Thane kill has a fixed rhythm.** ***SamFPlays***: *"Put on your mace, shield, and then you're going to do the air enchantment just so you attack faster."* ([Every Skip Explained, 5:38](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=338)). Enchant Weapon: Air sits at **Attack 30**.

**The Heart has two stances.** ***SamFPlays*** burns it with the staff from the third line: *"The third line here, just stand here, aim for the top of the heart. And left click."* ([10:40](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=640)). ***FastTipsGaming*** uses fire magic from range: *"While inside, my preferred method has always been fire magic."* ([Fight skip, 1:09](https://youtu.be/L-dTDXJyFq0?t=69)). ***Nanobit*** uses the **melee safespot**.

**The Dragon Scimitar** comes from your first clear: it *"can be received after completing the Scorned Wilderness raid and opening the Queenslayer's Reward Pack"* ([Dragon Scimitar, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Dragon_Scimitar)).

**Antipoison** is brewed from **Irit, Poison Ichor and a Glass Vessel** at a **Brewing Cauldron** ([Antipoison Potion, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Antipoison_Potion)). Carry one for the Heart on the hardcore-safe build.
**Nanobit's armour and food are a gap in the sources.** His quick-access slots hold his **helmet and pies**; his armour set is unstated, so match ***SamFPlays'*** mage armour.
What this means when you run

items: **Carry two Fleet-footed Infusions** and drink the second in the Stronghold.
**Hold a mace for the Thane** and swap to the 2H staff for the Heart.
**Wear a weapon with a plunge animation** for every dive cancel.

pages.title: What is a zoop in the Dragonwilds raid?
pages.summary: What is a zoop? A zoop is the long launch off an edge that carries you between Scorned Wilderness islands, timed to the single frame where the rock drops away.

body.text: A **zoop** is the **long launch off an edge** that carries you from one Scorned Wilderness island to the next, made by inputting the dash on the frame your character walks off the lip. It is the **most precise input** in the run and the **largest single source** of time between a 7:01 and a sub-7.

***Nanobit*** puts it at the centre of his run notes: the 7:01 *"needs very clean movement and strong zoops. Especially in the area with the 3rd BD directly after zooping from keep"* ([7:01 description](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0)).
What do you need to zoop?

rows: The dash you input at the edge
Recovery when a zoop comes up short

body.text: How do you zoop?
***Nanobit*** describes the timing for the hardest zoop in the run, **Vines to Fragments**:

items: **Walk or run** to the end of the flat part of the launch rock.
**Watch the lip.** The rock has *"an incredibly small slope after the flat part, before it drops off completely."*
**Input the dash** *"either on the frame you start walking off the rock … or 1 before."*
**Read the result.** *"Any earlier and you smash your ankles into the side Fragments and fall to your death, any later and it becomes an air dash."*
**Walk the approach** while you learn it. ***Nanobit*** found *"walking allows more time to react"*, with the same distance as running.

body.text: Load his [Vines to Fragments zoop at 1:45](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=105) **now** and step through the lip frame by frame.
Where does the route zoop?
These are the zoops ***Nanobit*** marks as time saves in his 7:01, at video time:

rows: "Technically could start zoop to Fragments about 1.5s earlier but this zoop is hard, so safety."
"can make it all the way to the gate with a good one, save maybe 2.5s"
"you can make it all the way to where I'm standing at 2:37, with no air/phase dash at all."
"This zoop can go far enough to require no dashes."
"This saves A LOT of time if it works."
"Sometimes this zoop is strong enough to only need 1 dash, then you can save the phase dash for Kuldra."
"With a strong enough zoop you don't need an air or phase dash."

body.text: **The pattern is consistent:** a strong zoop saves the dashes, and saved dashes buy time later at Kuldra.
Is there an easier Fragments skip?

**Yes.** ***Nanobit*** points learners to his slower, safer version: *"if you want an easier (but slower) skip to Fragments I suggest checking out my Day 1 Strats Video … for the zoop from necro island into respawn skip"* ([7:01 comment](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=105)). The day-one steps read: *"zoop left side off rocks left of bridge towards top of pillar on left, needs decent height, may or may not need both dashes depending on strength of zoop"* ([8:32 description](https://youtu.be/vw_Mr5TGJAg?t=0)).
**The skip itself traces to *SectorTSWG* via *Sir_Rebral*:** *"The skip to Fragments of Ghornfell I saw in a video by @SectorTSWG"* ([Sir_Rebral, 0:53](https://youtu.be/r1nrG2NlW-g?t=53)).
Does framerate change zoop distance?

**This is the open experiment of the route.** ***Nanobit***: *"I think lower framerates can give better zoops as well, just from random observations, but I can't/haven't really tested that."* ***Trance_OCE*** proposes the test: *"see if zooping and distance is tied to FPS (is the case on the tiger engine /destiny 2 and worldlining)"*.
**Run the test yourself:** cap your framerate at two values, take 20 zoops from the same rock at each, and mark the landing spot.
What this means when you run

items: **Walk the approach** to the Fragments zoop until the frame timing feels automatic.
**Learn the necro-island respawn version first** and switch to the direct zoop once it lands every time.
**Bank every dash a strong zoop saves** and spend it at Kuldra.

pages.title: What is the community sum of best for the Scorned Wilderness raid?
pages.summary: What is the community sum of best for the Scorned Wilderness raid? 6:38.27 at split level, built partly on patched strats. The pace that beats 6:50 today is 6:48.10.

body.text: The **community sum of best** is the total of the **fastest measured segment** for each of the five splits, taken from any record run: for the Scorned Wilderness raid it is **398.27 seconds, 6:38.27**. The **target pace** that beats the record on today's patch is **6:48.10**, built from pieces that still work on 1.0.1.2.
*(A **sum of best** is the time a perfect run would score if every split matched the best version seen.)*
What are the six measured runs?
Segment times in seconds, all on the same extraction-banner trigger (±0.1 s).

Bold marks the fastest segment in each column: 81.52 + 61.10 + 51.70 + 87.80 + 116.15 = **398.27 s**. ***TexasPete's*** 7:40 total is the measured cut to black; his on-screen timer stopped early, *"I accidently stopped the clock less than a second short. Total time was roughly 7.40.84"*.
Why is the target slower than the sum of best?

**The 6:38.27 includes patched pieces.** Its Stronghold segment is ***TexasPete's*** Thane-less wall climb, and both of its Sanctum-era runs climbed the blocks to Kuldra, which 1.0.1.2 closed. ***Nanobit***: *"Windstepping up the blocks to Kuldra no longer works as of 1.0.1.2/1.0.1.3."*

**The run path rebuilds the route from valid pieces.** Cut into 13 checkpoint pieces and kept to what works on 1.0.1.2, the fastest composite is **6:52.80**. The target takes **4.7 seconds** of named saves off it to reach **6:48.10**. The full method is in [the skip-level path](#/kb?p=post%3Askip-level-optimal-path).

What do the runners' own sums of best say?

**They agree with the target.** ***Nanobit*** on the 7:04: *"Overall just doing things more cleanly will produce a sub 7 considering my sum of best is 6:58."* On the 7:01: *"clearly can be done sub 7 judging by my sum of best"*. The Raid Lab dataset records his 7:01 sum of best as **6:51 (411 s)**.

pages.title: What is the fastest Scorned Wilderness speedrun route?
pages.summary: What is the fastest Scorned Wilderness route? It is Nanobit's 7:01 skeleton with Dotxy's Sanctum flight: five splits, every skip credited, timed against the 6:50.

body.text: **The fastest Scorned Wilderness speedrun route** is ***Nanobit's*** **7:01 route** *(the fastest run on the 1.0.1 ruleset)* with ***Dotxy's*** **Sanctum flight** in the final split. It carries you from the loading screen to the cut to black after Kuldra's Heart in **five splits**, and it **works on patch 1.0.1.2**.
This pillar teaches that route **one skip group at a time**, in the exact order you play it. Every skip names **who found it**, shows **where it happens** in a record run, and links the clip.
Why build on the 7:01 instead of the 6:50?

***TexasPete's*** **6:50** is the record to beat and the **best movement reference** in the game. Its route belongs to an earlier patch: ***Nanobit*** says it is *"using some strats that have been patched at this point"*.

***Nanobit's*** **7:01** runs the **1.0.1 route** that survives today, with one change he writes into his own description: *"Windstepping up the blocks to Kuldra no longer works as of 1.0.1.2/1.0.1.3. You can still get up to that area via just flying lmao."* That flight is ***Dotxy's*** tech, taught in the [Sanctum post](#/kb?p=post%3Akuldras-sanctum-flight-and-fight-skip).
What are the five splits?

**A split** is one timed section of the run. The community split file ends splits 1 to 4 on the **"EXTRACTION POINT UNLOCKED"** banner *(the message when you reach a Zilyana Teleporter)* and split 5 on the **cut to black** after "GET OUT NOW!", which is the speedrun.com end rule.

rows: One timed section of the run, ended by a fixed on-screen trigger.
A long launch off an edge that carries you between islands.
A route piece that bypasses the intended path, puzzle or fight.
The total of the fastest segment for every split.

body.text: Here is every split, measured **frame by frame** (±0.1 s) in the [Raid Lab](https://drthomasager.github.io/dragonwilds-speedrun/):
***TexasPete*** wins the **first three splits**. ***Nanobit*** wins the **Keep** and the **Sanctum**. The fastest segment from each adds up to **6:38.27**.
What is the route in play order?

items: **[Dragontail Vines](#/kb?p=post%3Adragontail-vines-split-route)**: the air anima Windstep, the soulscourge skip and the black dragon skip.
**[The skip to Fragments of Ghornfell](#/kb?p=post%3Askip-to-fragments-of-ghornfell)**: the zoop past the necromancer area, found by ***SectorTSWG*** via ***Sir_Rebral***.
**[Fragments of Ghornfell](#/kb?p=post%3Afragments-of-ghornfell-poison-and-abyssal-demon-skip)**: the poison area skip and the Abyssal Demon skip.
**[The Shattered Stronghold](#/kb?p=post%3Ashattered-stronghold-garou-thane-skip)**: ***Sir_Rebral's*** Garou Thane kill through the gate.
**[Cataclysm Keep](#/kb?p=post%3Acataclysm-keep-hole-elemental-puzzle-skip)**: the hole found by ***IINo1goodII*** and ***notmusty1***.
**[Kuldra's Sanctum](#/kb?p=post%3Akuldras-sanctum-flight-and-fight-skip)**: ***Dotxy's*** flight, the fight skip and the rib clip.
**[Kuldra's Heart](#/kb?p=post%3Akuldras-heart-where-to-stand)**: where to stand, and the cut to black.

body.text: Where is the time left?

***Nanobit*** names the place himself: *"Especially in the area with the 3rd BD directly after zooping from keep, if you get a strong enough one you can make it all the way from where you landed to well past the plant."*
**The biggest open save is the Sanctum.** Both record Sanctum segments **predate** ***Dotxy's*** **1.0.1.2 flight**, so a clean flight is the clearest path under 6:50.
What is the optimal path on 1.0.1.2?

**The optimal path** is the fastest chain of route pieces that still work on 1.0.1.2, timed **checkpoint to checkpoint** across four runs (about ±0.3 s, read from frame strips). It adds up to **6:52.80**. The **target pace** that beats the record is **6:48.10**, and the extra time comes mostly from the **Sanctum flight**, the **Heart safespot** and the **Keep**.

rows: Escape to the cut to black

body.text: **Test steps** are pieces still waiting for a timed 1.0.1.2 run: ***TexasPete's*** direct line to Fragments, ***FastTipsGaming's*** Stronghold launch and ***Dotxy's*** flight. Each post in this pillar gives the fallback.

**The pace shape is level, ahead, then hold.** Run level with the 6:50 through split 3, reach split 4 about **8 s ahead** thanks to the 1.0.1 Keep hole, give back about **6 s** in the Sanctum (the flight is slower than the patched blocks), and take about **4 s** back at the Heart. Taking the flight from about **52 s to 49 s** is what turns sub-6:50 into a routine target.
What this means when you run

items: **Learn the full route slowly first** with ***SamFPlays'*** [11-minute follow-along](https://youtu.be/WpvNjqVmpVM?t=0), then add one skip group per session.
**Copy TexasPete's movement** in splits 1 to 3 and **Nanobit's route** in splits 4 and 5.
**Check each skip's status** in [Patch Watch](#/kb?p=post%3Awhat-patch-1-0-1-2-changed-for-raid-speedruns) before every practice session.

pages.summary: What is the fastest skip-by-skip path through the Scorned Wilderness raid? A 6:52.80 composite of 13 pieces that all still work on 1.0.1.2, and a 6:48.10 pace built on it.

body.text: The **skip-level optimal path** is the fastest route through the Scorned Wilderness built from **13 checkpoint pieces**, each one the quickest version of that stretch that **still works on patch 1.0.1.2**. Stitched together, the pieces add up to **6:52.80**, and a **6:48.10** pace on top of them beats the record.

**Every existing run has a patched piece in it.** The 6:50 uses the old Keep skip, the Thane-less wall climb and the Windstep up the blocks to Kuldra; the 7:01 and SamFPlays' run also climb the blocks. So the path is built piece by piece, and every piece without a 1.0.1.2 run behind it is marked **unverified**.
How was the path measured?

**Frame by frame, on 15 checkpoints.** Each checkpoint time was *"read off contact sheets (1 frame / 2 s) and refined with 0.2 s strips (about +-0.3 s, about +-1 s on fuzzy visual checkpoints)"*. The checkpoints follow ***SamFPlays'*** chapters, so every run cuts at the same places.

rows: Fastest version of every piece, patched or not
Pieces that work on 1.0.1.2, three of them unverified
Proven 1.0.1.x pieces only: ***Nanobit's*** Fragments zoop and Thane kill, ***Dotxy's*** flight
The composite minus 4.7 s of named saves

body.text: What is the 1.0.1.2 composite?

**Credits for the pieces:** the Keep hole belongs to ***IINo1goodII*** and ***notmusty1***, the rib clip to ***wes7918***, the flight to ***Dotxy***, the Thane launch to ***FastTipsGaming***. The strict fallbacks are ***SectorTSWG's*** Fragments skip via ***Sir_Rebral*** and ***Sir_Rebral's*** Thane kill.
What are the three unverified pieces?

items: **The TexasPete line to Fragments** (9.5 s): straight off the black dragon ledge, a 1.0.0.6-era line that no 1.0.1 runner has shown. **Fallback:** ***Nanobit's*** vines zoop, 15.6 s.

**The FastTipsGaming Thane launch** (51.9 s): no Thane kill; climb the rocks left of the air door, Windstep and glide into the forest. It comes from a full raid posted on 2 November, after 1.0.1.2, timed at tutorial pace. **Fallback:** ***Nanobit's*** Thane kill and air door, 63.1 s.
**The Dotxy flight** (51.9 s): a demo, which lands and walks the walkway mid-way. **It replaces the blocks route**, 35.0 s in both records, which 1.0.1.2 closed.

body.text: **Test each unverified piece** three times on 1.0.1.2 before you route it.
What pace beats 6:50 on this path?
The target is **6:48.10**: the composite minus **4.7 seconds** of named saves.
**Where the 4.7 seconds come from:**

items: **Sanctum flight, 51.9 to 49.0 s.** A direct flight line skips the demo's walk.
**Heart, 46.0 to 42.5 s.** ***Nanobit*** *"slightly missed the melee safespot"*; hit it first time.
**Keep, 75.2 to 73.5 s.** Plunge cancels at 5:07 and 5:12, no extra rock jump, an instant rib clip.

body.text: **The pace shape:** level with the 6:50 through S3, about **8 s ahead at S4** thanks to the Keep hole, then about **6 s back in the Sanctum**, because flight is slower than the patched blocks. **The Sanctum flight is the swing segment.**
Which saves matter most against a follow-along run?
Measured against ***SamFPlays'*** 1.0.1 follow-along route:

rows: **Keep hole + rib clip** instead of the elemental puzzle
**Melee heart safespot** instead of a mage staff
**Zoop to Fragments** instead of the death warp
**Poison hole + demon Surge**, cleaner portal line

body.text: What this means when you run

items: **Load the 6:48.10 split targets** into your timer and race them every attempt.
**Test the three unverified pieces** on 1.0.1.2, keeping the fallback for each.
**Drill the Sanctum flight** toward 49.0 s door to tunnel, the swing segment.

pages.title: What is the infinite double jump in Dragonwilds?
pages.summary: What is the infinite double jump? It is Dotxy's flight loop: Windstep once, then Jump Attack, spell ring, AoE spell, Escape, Jump, repeated.

body.text: The **infinite double jump** is ***Dotxy's*** loop of **dive cancels and air jumps** that keeps you airborne for as long as you hold the rhythm; chained through Kuldra's Sanctum it is called **Sanctum flight**. It is the route's answer to patch 1.0.1.2.

**This is the swing segment of the record.** Both record runs climbed the blocks from the Sanctum door to the heart tunnel in **35.0 s**, a route 1.0.1.2 closed. ***Dotxy's*** flight demo covers the same stretch in **51.9 s**, and the 6:48.10 target pace asks for **49.0 s**. Every second of flight you save goes straight off the run.
Why does the route need flight?

**Patch 1.0.1.2 closed the old way up.** ***Nanobit***: *"Windstepping up the blocks to Kuldra no longer works as of 1.0.1.2/1.0.1.3. You can still get up to that area via just flying lmao."* ([7:01 description](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0))

***Dotxy* posted flight the same day as the patch:** *"here's a new way to get through Kuldra's Sanctum quick in the Runescape Dragonwilds 1.0.1.2 hotfix!"* ([Sanctum flight](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0))
What do you need to fly?
How do you do the loop?
***Dotxy's*** inputs, verbatim from his description:

items: **Windstep**
**Jump Attack**
**Q (Spell Ring)**
**[any targeted aoe spell]**
**Escape** (closes Spell Ring interface)
**Jump**

body.text: *"Repeat steps 2-6 as needed!"* Windstep starts the loop once; steps 2 to 6 repeat.
**Speed gains height.** ***Dotxy***: *"If you're faster than I am you can gain height, not just hover lol"* ([Infinite Double Jump](https://youtu.be/goKfbT19nkk?t=0)).
**Dashes mix in.** ***IINo1goodII***: *"btw i'm sure you know you can dash n phase dash doing this too."* ([comment](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0))
Load the [90-second flight](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0) **now** and run the loop on flat ground until it hovers.
How do you do it on console?
**It works on console.** ***IINo1goodII***: *"I've been doing this consistently on console."* ***brendonboyd7668*** shares a PS5 layout:

items: *"Set your spell wheel to where wind step is Triangle R1 input. Set your repair equipment spell to Traingle R2 for Righties or L2 for lefties."*
*"Start off by practicing this pattern Repair Spell, Cancel spell, double jump R1"*
*"Add wind step to the beginning of the pattern"*

body.text: *"You don't need to re input windstep after the first time just keep the pattern from Step 2."* ([comment](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0))
Can you use a macro?

**Ask the moderators first.** ***Dotxy*** suggests one: *"Feel free to set up a macro for easy infinite flight!"* The speedrun.com raid rules state the timing and video requirements and are silent on macros. **Message *Archy* or *dotyoureyes* before you submit a run that uses one.**
Does it still work today?

**Yes, as of 2 November 2026.** ***FastTipsGaming*** posted *"my full unedited Kuldra raid and boss skip in Runescape Dragonwilds"* ([full raid](https://youtu.be/oK0_U_I40DY?t=0)) using the infinite-jump cycle, plus a tutorial ([Infinite Jump EXPLOIT](https://youtu.be/U0_KPXu28qw?t=0)).
What this means when you run

items: **Drill steps 2 to 6** on flat ground until you climb instead of hover.
**Fly the Sanctum in practice** and race the door-to-tunnel stretch against the 49.0 s target.
**Confirm the macro ruling** with the moderators before any submitted run.

pages.title: What movement tech do you need for the Dragonwilds raid?
pages.summary: What movement tech do you need for the Scorned Wilderness raid? Five primitives: the zoop, the dive cancel, infinite double jump, Surge plus Phase Dash and the windjump.

body.text: **Movement tech** is the set of **movement primitives** *(short, repeatable input sequences that move you further or faster than the intended path)* that every Scorned Wilderness skip is built from. Five primitives cover the whole 1.0.1.2 route: the **zoop**, the **dive cancel**, the **infinite double jump**, **Surge plus Phase Dash** and the **windjump**.

**The record lives in this pillar.** ***Nanobit*** names the requirement for a sub-7 directly: the run *"needs very clean movement and strong zoops"* ([7:01 description](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0)).
Why does movement decide the record?

**Patch 1.0.1 changed the movement kit.** Jagex added the **Jump Attack** and confirmed it works off Windstep: *"And yes, Windstep counts here. What goes up, must come crashing down."* ([1.0.1 patch notes](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1846651706673783))

**The same day, *Dotxy* turned it into a cancel**, and within nine days the cancel became **flight**. ***Nanobit*** sums up the arc: *"Plunge-cancel tech has evolved even further"* ([7:01 description](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0)).

**The 6:50 predates all of it.** ***TexasPete*** recorded it *"prior to the windstep double jump and some other new routing strats"* ([6:50 description](https://youtu.be/6WEIHo7AUf0?t=0)). The new primitives are **where the time below 6:50 comes from**.
What are the five primitives?

rows: A long launch off an edge between islands, timed to one frame
A targeted AoE cast that ends the Jump Attack animation instantly
Chained dive cancels and air jumps; through the Sanctum it is **flight**
[What is the infinite double jump in Dragonwilds?](#/kb?p=post%3Ainfinite-double-jump-sanctum-flight)
Surge dodges chained with extra air dashes for long horizontal distance
[How does the Surge and Phase Dash combo work?](#/kb?p=post%3Asurge-and-phase-dash-combo)
A Windstep jump onto ledges; a clip through the ground at Kuldra's checkpoint
[What are the windjump and the rib clip?](#/kb?p=post%3Awindjump-and-rib-clip)

body.text: In what order should you learn them?

items: **Windjump first.** It needs only **Windstep** (Agility 5) and it appears in every split.
**Surge plus Phase Dash second.** It powers the **Abyssal Demon** skip and the **Sanctum approach**.
**Dive cancel third.** It is the **building block** of flight.
**Infinite double jump fourth.** It turns the dive cancel into **Sanctum flight**, the swing segment of a sub-6:50.
**Zoops last.** They are the **most precise** inputs in the run and they repay hundreds of attempts.

body.text: What this means when you run

items: **Practise the windjump** on every ledge you meet until it lands first time.
**Learn the dive cancel on flat ground** before you take it into the Sanctum.
**Save zoops for last** and give them their own practice block every session.

pages.title: What should you set up before every raid attempt?
pages.summary: What should you set up before a raid attempt? Full rest, full hydration, a bed at Rasthin's Rest, ring keybinds, a respawned Air Thane, tested settings and the five-split timer.

body.text: **The pre-run setup** is the **checklist you clear at Rasthin's Rest** before you talk to Commander Zilyana: **full rest**, **full hydration**, **bed spawn**, **keybinds**, **settings**, a **respawned Air Thane** and a **timer** that splits where speedrun.com does.
Every item on it **protects stamina, time or a split**.
What is on the checklist?

rows: Rest, hydration and sustenance stop dwindling
Deaths return you to the start line
Cancel spell slot 1, Surge 3, Phase Dash 4, Windstep 7
Two Fleet-footed Infusions, Strong Tea, mace, staff, runes
HUD visible, game audio on, recording started
Five splits, banner and cut-to-black triggers

body.text: How do you set up the bed?

**The bed** needs **8 ash planks and 4 rough cloth**, and *"must be under a roof and enclosed with three walls to be used"* ([Bed, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Bed)). ***SamFPlays*** builds his right at the start: *"put a bed right here. Look at that janky roof, put a bed there. That way when you die you respawn right here."* ([Every Skip Explained, 1:43](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=103)).
Why sleep right before the run?

**Rest caps your stamina.** The wiki's thresholds: **50 Tired** limits stamina to **80**, **25 Knackered** to **60**, **0 Exhausted** to **40** ([Rest, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Rest)). A full night's sleep also grants **Fresh Start**, a **180-second** buff that stops rest, hydration and sustenance dwindling.

**Sleep at Rasthin's Rest**, then start the run while Fresh Start covers the opening splits. Since 1.0.0.5, *"Summon Shelter will be able to be used in the Scorned Wilderness hub"* ([1.0.0.5 notes, Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1844751498218499)).
Why drink to full hydration?

**Hydration sets stamina regen.** At **100 hydration** stamina regenerates at **6.0 per second**; at **0** it regenerates at **0.75** ([Hydration, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Hydration)). **Drink clean water** before entering; dirty water builds toward **Soulscourge**.
Why check the Air Thane?

**The air Garou Thane** is a kill on the Stronghold route, and ***Nanobit*** found his respawn is slow: *"Air Thane takes like 15 minutes to respawn, it's best to just sleep through a night after completing a run... otherwise he doesn't spawn in the next run and ruins your time."* ([8:32 run, description](https://youtu.be/vw_Mr5TGJAg?t=0)).

**Sleep through a night between attempts.** One night covers **rest**, **Fresh Start** and **the Thane** together. Jagex's 1.0.1 notes add that *"Obstacles and Enemies now respawn in the Scorned Wildnerness Raid on reset/next run-through"* ([1.0.1 notes, Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1846651706673783)); **check the Thane is standing** in the air room before you commit to the gate kill.
Which keybinds speed up the run?

**Every spell goes through the ring.** The wiki: players *"can access their customised spellbooks by pressing the Q-button (default)"* ([Magic, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Magic)). Pressing **Q then a number** picks a ring slot in one motion.

***Nanobit***: *"I'm using Q1E for the plunge-cancel tech, and Q7 a lot of the time to windstep. However sometimes it's better to just cast normally if you're doing multiple casts, since you can just spam click to hit the next spell ASAP."* ([reply on the 7:01](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0)). **Test what the final `E` does** in your own setup: ***Dotxy*** closes the ring with `Esc` instead.

**Number keys without the ring fire quick-access slots.** ***Nanobit***: *"I find spamming Q3/Q4 just equips my helmet and eats my pies when I don't want to, most of the time."* **Keep your quick-access slots clear of anything you mind triggering.**

**Hold sprint once.** ***Nanobit*** lost time at the start: *"Tapped sprint in beginning but was already sprinting, so walked in beginning for about 1.5s before re-sprinting"* ([7:01, 0:23](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=23)).
Console layouts are in the [console inputs post](#/kb?p=post%3Aconsole-inputs-for-raid-tech).
Which settings should you test?
**No runner has published their settings.** Run each as a **test step**: change one, run ten attempts of the Fragments zoop, and log the make rate.

rows: Which one sends Surge where you aim
Camera stability during the Jump Attack

body.text: **Framerate is the strongest lead.** ***Nanobit***: *"I think lower framerates can give better zoops as well, just from random observations, but I can't/haven't really tested that."* ([comment on the 7:01](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=105)). The option list comes from the wiki's Settings page: *"Frame Rate Limit: Dynamic (default), 30, 60, 90, 120, 140 frames per second"* ([Settings, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Settings)). **Lock the cap you choose** so every session compares cleanly.
How should your timer and recording work?

**Match the speedrun.com rule.** The timer starts *"the first frame the loading icon disappears going into the raid"* and ends *"on the frame the screen goes black after the "Get out now!" timer ends after defeating Kuldra's Heart"* ([speedrun.com Raid rules](https://www.speedrun.com/Runescape_Dragonwilds)).

**Use the community five-split file**: Dragontail Vines, Fragments of Ghornfell, The Shattered Stronghold, Cataclysm Keep, Kuldra's Sanctum. **Target splits** for a 6:48 run are **1:22.70**, **2:23.20**, **3:15.70**, **4:42.30** and **6:48.10** (Raid Lab run path).

**Record full video with game audio** and keep the HUD visible: the game rules require *"a full video of the run, including game audio"* and state that *"Dynamic HUD elements should not be obscured or omitted (e.g. health, inventory, stamina)"*. **Start recording a few seconds early.** A moderator told ***ChiefWes***: *"make sure to start the recording a couple seconds sooner right before you go into the raid."* ([speedrun.com run](https://www.speedrun.com/Runescape_Dragonwilds/runs/z146l1wz)).
What this means when you run

items: **Sleep at Rasthin's Rest** before every attempt to refill rest, start Fresh Start and respawn the air Garou Thane.
**Bind the ring the way the runners do**: cancel spell on 1, Surge on 3, Phase Dash on 4, Windstep on 7.
**Lock your framerate cap and start recording early** with game audio and the HUD visible.

pages.title: Where do you stand to kill Kuldra's Heart fast?
pages.summary: Where do you stand at Kuldra's Heart? Jump straight into the melee safespot the records use, about 45 seconds faster than a mage staff from range, then escape before the cut to black.

body.text: **Kuldra's Heart** is the **final target** of the raid, inside Kuldra, and the run ends on the frame the screen goes **black after the "Get out now!" timer** that starts when the Heart dies. The record finish is the **melee safespot** *(a standing spot beside the Heart where you take no hits)*, which ***TexasPete*** brought to the route and ***Nanobit*** uses in his 7:01.

The Heart is a **DPS check** *(a fight decided by how much damage you deal per second)*, and **heartworms** *(parasites with 753 HP that keep respawning in the chamber)* guard it. The melee safespot finishes it in about **46 s**. ***SamFPlays'*** magic spot with a 2H mage staff takes about **92 s** and is the calm way to learn the room.
What do you need?
See [What gear do you bring?](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-gear-and-consumables) and [Which spells and perks do raid skips use?](#/kb?p=post%3Aspells-and-perks-for-raid-skips)
Where is the melee safespot?
**The melee Heart** is ***TexasPete's*** idea, credited by ***Nanobit***. ***Nanobit*** slightly missed the safespot at 6:47 in his 7:01 and jumped in correctly at **6:53**, about **6 s** lost.

items: **Leave the Heart tunnel** and jump straight into the safespot along the line ***Nanobit*** takes at [6:53](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=413).
**Burn the Heart** from there.
**Run for the exit** the moment "Get out now!" appears: the timer runs until the screen goes black.

body.text: Where do you stand with magic?
**Stand back at the edge.** Three runners describe the same spot:

items: **Follow ***SamFPlays'*** standing spot** from his chapter [Where to stand so heartworms don't spawn](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=637).

**Stay up on the edge** and cast at the Heart from there. ***southpark159753***: *"You can stand back and hit the heart with magic, doesnt start the fight with worms. Like dont drop down into the area."*
**Hold your spot close to the edge.** ***beandon*** explains the reason: standing too far in lets a tentacle spawn on you.

body.text: How fast is the Heart?
**The Heart is timed in two pieces** (about ±0.3 s): from the **Heart tunnel load** to the **"GET OUT NOW" banner**, then from the banner to the **cut to black**.

rows: Escape to the cut to black

body.text: **The melee safespot saves 45.6 s** against the mage staff from range. **The target is 42.5 s**: ***Nanobit's*** 46.0 s with the safespot entered first time. **The escape is fixed** at about 13.8 to 14.2 s in every run, so the time to gain lives in the Heart itself.
Does it work on 1.0.1.2?
**Both spots work on 1.0.1.2.** ***beandon*** posted his edge advice on 27 October and ***southpark159753*** his magic spot after the patch went live.
What this means when you run

items: **Jump straight into the melee safespot** on your first try: that is 6 s against the 7:01.
**Learn the room with the magic spot** at the edge, then switch to melee for timed runs.
**Run the moment the Heart dies**: the escape is a fixed 14 s and the clock stops on the cut to black.

pages.title: Where does TexasPete's 6:50 beat Nanobit's 7:01?
pages.summary: Where does TexasPete's 6:50 beat Nanobit's 7:01? In Vines, Fragments and the Stronghold, by 23.7 seconds. Nanobit wins the Keep and the Sanctum by 11.73.

body.text: The **6:50 versus the 7:01** is the comparison of the top two Scorned Wilderness runs on one shared trigger: ***TexasPete*** gains **23.7 seconds** in the first three splits, and ***Nanobit*** takes back **11.73 seconds** in Cataclysm Keep and Kuldra's Sanctum. The record margin is **11.97 seconds**.

**The two runs sit on different patches.** ***TexasPete*** played on 14 October, *"prior to the windstep double jump and some other new routing strats"*; ***Nanobit*** ran 1.0.1/1.0.1.1 and notes the 6:50 *"is using some strats that have been patched at this point"*.
How do the splits compare?
Segment times in seconds, measured on the extraction banner (±0.1 s). A negative delta means TexasPete is faster.
Where does each split start in the videos?
Open both links for one split **now** and watch them side by side.
Why is TexasPete faster early?

**The Stronghold holds the biggest gap: 11.4 seconds.** ***Nanobit*** names his own losses there: an *"Extra swing, not ideal"* at the Thane and a forgotten infusion, *"Don't forget to re-use your fleet-footed infusion here, because I did."* ([3:22](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=202)). ***Sir_Rebral*** saw the same moment: *"the extra hit after the Thane kill broke my heart haha"*.

**TexasPete commits to the big jumps.** His commentary at the Keep needle: *"Here at the needle."* ([4:27](https://youtu.be/6WEIHo7AUf0?t=267)), then *"I'm going to risk it all"* ([5:28](https://youtu.be/6WEIHo7AUf0?t=328)). Some of those landings are gone on 1.0.1.2; ***Keimbho***: *"the new update made the rock a phantom."*
Why is Nanobit faster late?

**The hole in Keep.** ***Nanobit*** thanks ***notmusty1*** via ***IINo1goodII*** *"for finding a lovely hole in Keep!"*, and his Keep through that hole is **8.5 seconds** faster than TexasPete's. In the Sanctum he wins **3.23 seconds**. Both Sanctum segments climb the blocks to Kuldra, which 1.0.1.2 closed, so a run today flies that stretch with ***Dotxy's*** loop.
What this means when you run

items: **Match TexasPete's pace** through the Stronghold with today's skips.
**Take Nanobit's Keep hole** and his Sanctum line for the back half.
**Bank 8 seconds by the Keep exit**, because flight gives about 6 back in the Sanctum.

pages.title: Where is the Scorned Wilderness world record won?
pages.summary: Where is the Scorned Wilderness record won? TexasPete's 6:50 wins the first three splits; Nanobit's 7:01 wins Cataclysm Keep and Kuldra's Sanctum.

body.text: The **Scorned Wilderness world record** is ***TexasPete's*** **6:50.000**, and it is won in the **first three splits**: he reaches the Keep **23.7 seconds** ahead of ***Nanobit's*** 7:01, then gives back **11.73 seconds** in Cataclysm Keep and Kuldra's Sanctum. This pillar measures every second of that, and turns it into **a pace you can run with**.
**Every number here is measured frame by frame**, on one shared trigger, so the runs compare directly.
How were the splits measured?

**One trigger, every run.** Splits 1 to 4 sit on the first frame the **"EXTRACTION POINT UNLOCKED"** banner shows. Split 5 is the **cut to black after "GET OUT NOW!"**, which is speedrun.com's end rule.

rows: Template matching at 10 fps, then checked frame by frame
The video second where the run timer reads 0, read from the on-screen timer at 3+ frames (agreement ±0.02 s)
Any mark can be adjusted in the Raid Lab (Race the WR, Adjust marks) and exported

body.text: What does the leaderboard look like?
**Zero runs await verification** in the Raid category as of 3 November 2026. The last Raid submission was the 6:50 itself.

body.text: Is there a faster run the board has yet to see?

**There is one unverified lead.** ***IINo1goodII*** posted *"Kuldra skipped in 4 mins 40 seconds"* on 28 October and writes *"Sub 4 mins is possible. I'm confident someone could do it in around 3 minutes flat."* ([video](https://youtu.be/4hncfjhUvg8?t=0)). He keeps the method private: *"Not showing full clip or methods used.. sorry guys."*

His comment names three pieces: *"I launched myself skipping the 3rd checkpoint and some of the parkour area. Used the plunge mech to bypass the rocks on the fight itself since they are patched. Surge dashed the bridge."* The run sits outside speedrun.com and its timing method is unpublished. **Ask in the RSDW Speedrunning Discord** ([invite](https://discord.gg/aGZkuC5yK6)), the hub ***Nanobit*** points runners to.
What this means when you run

items: **Bank time early**: the record is built in Vines, Fragments and the Stronghold.
**Race your splits** against both records on the same trigger in the Raid Lab.
**Chase the 4:40 lead** in the Discord and test each of its three pieces.

pages.title: Which Agility levels do you need for raid skips?
pages.summary: Which Agility levels do you need for raid skips? Agility 44 covers Windstep, Double Jump, Air Dash and Phase Dash; Agility 70 adds Reactive Recall for practice.

body.text: **Agility** is the skill that owns the **movement kit** in RuneScape: Dragonwilds. Jagex added it in 0.12.1, built *"to make you faster, leaner and meaner"* ([0.12.1 notes, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Update:0.12.1_is_now_live!)), and every 1.0.1+ raid skip uses at least one of its unlocks.
**Train Agility to 44** for the full route and **to 70** for a safety net while you practise.
Which unlocks does the route use?

rows: Air vent, Thane door, flight start

body.text: Values come from the wiki's Agility table and spell pages ([Agility](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Agility)).
What does Windstep need?

**Windstep** is the spell that makes you **jump up to 16 metres** and **fall more slowly**, with a **7-second window** to use it after casting ([Windstep, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Windstep)). It is the **first input** of ***Dotxy's*** flight loop and of ***Sir_Rebral's*** Thane-door windjump.

**The sources give two levels.** The Agility unlock table lists **Agility 5**; the Windstep infobox shows **level 8**, carried over from its Runecrafting days. Jagex moved it in 0.12.1: *"Windstep is now an Agility skill spell, rather than a Runecrafting skill spell."* ([0.12.1 notes, Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1839676055882020)). **Reach Agility 8** and both readings are covered.
**Leggings of Lightness** make Windstep cost **zero runes** ([gear post](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-gear-and-consumables)).
What do Double Jump and Hopper add?

**Double Jump** is a **second jump in mid-air**, up to **4 metres**, with **no cooldown** and the same **10 stamina** as a normal jump ([Double Jump, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Double_Jump)). ***Dotxy's*** infinite double jump chains it after every Jump Attack cancel. **Hopper** at 22 makes each jump **cheaper**.
What does Air Dash add?

**Air Dash** is the **10-metre horizontal dash** you get by pressing **evade while airborne** ([Air Dash, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Air_Dash)). ***Nanobit*** counts them in his run notes: *"Can do 4 air dash instead of 3 towards 1st air anima pillar"* ([7:01, 0:51](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=51)).
What does Phase Dash add?

**Phase Dash** grants **extra Air Dashes while airborne, up to 3 per cast**, for **20 Air + 10 Astral** runes on a **45-second cooldown** ([Phase Dash, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Phase_Dash)). ***SamFPlays*** pairs it with Surge to clear the **Abyssal Demon** ([Phase Dash & Surge combo, 0:00](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=0)). ***Nanobit*** spends it like a budget: *"then you can save the phase dash for Kuldra"* ([7:01, 5:18](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=318)).
What do Recall and Reactive Recall add?

**Recall** places a **runic marker**; recast to **teleport back**. At **Agility 70**, **Reactive Recall** fires **automatically on a fatal fall** and consumes the tether ([Reactive Recall, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Reactive_Recall)). Use it in **practice** to retry a vertical skip at once. The 0.12.1 notes keep Breakfall honest: *"Fatal falls will still kill you though."*
How do you train Agility?

items: **Sprint everywhere.** The wiki lists **foot travel**, **courses**, **dodging vault traps** and **dodging enemy attacks** as XP sources ([Agility](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Agility)).
**Run the agility courses** in each region as you pass them.

**Follow the phase order**: Windstep and Double Jump in **Phase 0**, Air Dash in **Phase 2**, Phase Dash in **Phase 3**, Recall in **Phase 4**, Reactive Recall in **Phase 5** of the Raid Lab Hardcore route.

body.text: **Travel on foot pays more as you level.** The wiki: *"Players will gain 50/200/400 Agility XP at level 1/48/85, passively simply by running on foot across the world."* ([Agility, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Agility)). The **Brynmoor courses** open at **Agility 1**, so the first course is available from your first hour.

**Fund the runes as you train.** Windstep and Phase Dash use **Air runes** (Runecrafting 1) and Phase Dash adds **Astral runes** (Runecrafting 3). Recall adds **Law runes**: the wiki states *"Law runes can be crafted at a rune altar at level 50 Runecrafting or higher"* ([Law Rune, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Law_Rune)), while the Hardcore route lists Runecrafting 16. **Check the Law altar level in-game**, and collect Law runes from **Garou Packs** (5 to 10 at a 10/100 rate) in the meantime ([Garou Pack, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Garou_Pack)).
What this means when you run

items: **Hit Agility 44** so Phase Dash is ready for the Abyssal Demon and the Kuldra approach.
**Count your dashes** per gap the way ***Nanobit*** does, and save Phase Dash for the end.
**Practise with Reactive Recall** at Agility 70 so missed vertical skips cost seconds.

pages.title: Which drills make every raid skip consistent?
pages.summary: Which drills make every raid skip consistent? One drill per skip, in split order, each looped against its reference clip and logged as made or missed.

body.text: **A skip drill** is **one skip, repeated in isolation**, with its **reference clip** looping beside you and **every attempt logged** as made or missed. The drill list below covers **every skip on the 1.0.1.2 route**, in split order, with the finder credited and the clip linked.
How do you run a drill?

items: **Open the skip's reference clip** and watch it **twice at full speed**.
**Load into the split** that holds the skip.
**Attempt the skip**, then **log it**: made or missed.
**Repeat** for a fixed block of attempts.
**Move to the next weakest skip** when the block ends.

body.text: In the ***Raid Lab*** Practice page you **loop the clip** and log with **J** (made) and **K** (missed). It tracks **consistency per skip** and **suggests your weakest skip next** ([Raid Lab](https://drthomasager.github.io/dragonwilds-speedrun/)).
Which skips go on the drill list?

rows: Windstep to the first air anima
Surge + Phase Dash past the Abyssal Demon
Garou Thane kill and air door

body.text: Which skip do you drill first?
**Start with the movement tech.** ***Dotxy's*** **dive cancel** and **infinite double jump** feed the Sanctum flight, so drilling them on flat ground first makes the Sanctum drill short.

**Then drill the Fragments zoop.** ***Nanobit*** names it the precise one: *"You need to use it either on the frame you start walking off the rock... or 1 before."* ([comment on the 7:01](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=105)). He offers an easier fallback: *"if you want an easier (but slower) skip to Fragments I suggest checking out my Day 1 Strats Video"* ([8:32 run](https://youtu.be/vw_Mr5TGJAg?t=0)). **Drill the fallback until it is automatic**, then drill the fast version.
How do you turn drills into runs?

**Use the timer and the race view.** The ***Raid Lab*** Timer behaves like LiveSplit, with **golds** and **PB**, and exports a `.lss` with the **WR**, ***Nanobit*** and the **community sum of best** as comparisons. It also **imports `.lss` history** to show **where your runs die**. **Race the WR** plays your run beside the 6:50 on one run clock.
**The run navigator** has **segment practice**: start the clock at any split, run that segment, and the result joins your history.
What does a missed skip cost?

**Each miss has a price in seconds.** The Raid Lab model assigns a **time loss per miss** to every skip. Two of them are **measured** from the run path (the Keep puzzle and the Heart re-entry); the rest are **modelled estimates** of the recovery.

rows: Drop out of the loop and climb again
Walk part of the poison area

body.text: ***Nanobit's*** own note is the Heart measurement: *"I slightly missed the melee safespot, I jump into it correctly at 6:53."* ([7:01, 6:47](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=407)).
What make rate should you aim for?

**Aim for 90% or better on every skip, and drill the expensive ones first.** The Raid Lab practice model ranks drills by how much each one raises your chance of a sub-6:50. Its worked example uses a **synthetic new-runner profile** (generated practice logs, clearly labelled as not real data), so read the ranking as an **order of work** and set your own numbers from your own J/K logs.

columns: Clean reps the model asks for

body.text: **The targets halve the miss rate.** Every row in the model's plan is the same move: cut misses in half on one skip, then re-rank.

**Pace matters as much as make rate.** In the Raid Lab simulation (20,000 runs per route), the current-patch route with ***Dotxy's*** flight and ***Nanobit's*** Keep hole, run at ***TexasPete's*** calibrated pace, has a median of **7:31.95** and a best 1-in-1,000 run of **7:11.44**. The 6:48 run path closes that gap with **faster pieces**: ***TexasPete's*** Fragments line, ***FastTipsGaming's*** Thane launch and a flight about **3 s** faster than ***Dotxy's*** demo. **Drill those pieces for speed once your make rates sit above 90%.**
What this means when you run

items: **Drill the movement tech first**, then the Fragments zoop, then the rest in split order.
**Log every attempt** with J and K so the weakest skip picks itself.
**Import your `.lss` history** to find the split where your runs die.

pages.title: Which inputs work on console for raid tech?
pages.summary: Which inputs work on console for raid tech? Put only Windstep and Magical Mending on one spell radial, map them to Triangle plus L1 and L2, slam with R1 and jump with X.

body.text: **Raid tech inputs** are the **button layouts** that let you fire ***Dotxy's*** cancel loop and the Surge and dash chains **fast enough** to gain height. On console the loop runs through a **spell radial**; on PC it runs through **Q plus a number key**.

**The loop is learnable on console.** ***IINo1goodII***: *"I've been doing this consistently on console. btw i'm sure you know you can dash n phase dash doing this too."* ([comment on Sanctum flight](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0)). ***FastTipsGaming*** completed a **full unedited raid and boss skip** on the current patch with it on 2 November ([full run](https://youtu.be/oK0_U_I40DY?t=0)).
What is the loop you are mapping?

rows: Closes the ring, cancels the cast

body.text: ***Dotxy***: *"Repeat steps 2-6 as needed!"* ([Sanctum flight, description](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0)). Speed matters: *"If you're faster than I am you can gain height, not just hover lol"* ([Infinite Double Jump](https://youtu.be/goKfbT19nkk?t=0)).
What do you need for it?

***FastTipsGaming***: *"The only thing you need is access to a melee weapon, two spells, and enough runes to cast them."* ([Infinite Jump, 0:06](https://youtu.be/U0_KPXu28qw?t=6)). The two spells are **Windstep** and the cancel spell, and he names the default: *"Everyone pretty much agrees that magical mending is the best one to use because most people unlock it earlier than the others."* ([0:17](https://youtu.be/U0_KPXu28qw?t=17)).
How do you set it up on PlayStation?
***FastTipsGaming's*** layout:

items: **Clear one spell radial**: *"clear some room in one of your spell radials and place only two spells, wind step and magic mending."* ([1:06](https://youtu.be/U0_KPXu28qw?t=66))
**Windstep** on **Triangle + L1**, then **X** to jump.
At the height of the jump, **R1** for the slam (Jump Attack).
**Triangle** at the very start of the slam, then **L2** to cast **Magical Mending**, which cancels the slam.
**L2 again** to cancel the spell.
**X** to jump, and repeat from step 3.

body.text: In his words: *"press triangle then L1. This simply gives you wind step. Then press X to jump ... at the height of your jump, press R1 to do a slam attack. ... press triangle in the very beginning of our slam attack ... Press L2 to activate the spell magical mending, which also cancels out your slam attack. ... After activating magical mending, press L2 again to cancel the spell. ... simply press X again to jump."* ([1:35](https://youtu.be/U0_KPXu28qw?t=95))

rows: Triangle + R2, or L2 left-handed (repair equipment spell)

body.text: ***brendonboyd7668***: *"Set your spell wheel to where wind step is Triangle R1 input. Set your repair equipment spell to Traingle R2 for Righties or L2 for lefties."* and *"You don't need to re input windstep after the first time just keep the pattern from Step 2."* ([comment on Sanctum flight](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0)).
**Xbox players** use the same positions on the matching Xbox buttons; no Xbox runner has published a layout yet, so **test your mapping** on flat ground first.
How do you set it up on PC?

**Use Q plus a number key.** ***Nanobit***: *"I'm using Q1E for the plunge-cancel tech, and Q7 a lot of the time to windstep."* ([reply on the 7:01](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0)). ***loopuleasa***: *"I spam Q+3 and Q+4 to enable surge and dash"* ([comment on the 7:01](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0)). The full PC table is in the [setup checklist](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-setup-checklist).
Can you use a macro?

**Ask the moderators first.** ***Dotxy*** suggests one: *"Feel free to set up a macro for easy infinite flight!"* ([Sanctum flight](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=0)). The speedrun.com Raid rules cover **timing** and the game rules cover **video** and **good faith**: *"Runs are expected to be performed in good faith and may be rejected based on mod discretion if performed otherwise."* ([speedrun.com](https://www.speedrun.com/Runescape_Dragonwilds)). **Message the moderators, Archy and dotyoureyes**, and get a written answer before you submit a macro run.
How do you build the rhythm?

items: **Drill the cancel on flat ground**: slam, cast, cancel, jump.
**Count the loop out loud** until it is even.
**Add Windstep** and aim to **gain height** each cycle.
**Mix in a dash or Phase Dash**, as ***IINo1goodII*** describes.
**Watch for autosaves.** ***FastTipsGaming***: *"If the game auto saves while you're trying to perform this trick, you're going down."* ([0:57](https://youtu.be/U0_KPXu28qw?t=57))
**Move to the Sanctum** once you climb on most loops.

body.text: What this means when you run

items: **Put only Windstep and Magical Mending on one radial** so the loop runs with one hand shape.
**Drill the cancel rhythm on flat ground** before you add Windstep.
**Get a written moderator answer** before you submit a run that uses a macro.

pages.title: Which spells and perks do raid skips use?
pages.summary: Which spells and perks do raid skips use? Surge at Magic 11, the Death From Above! Jump Attack at Attack 25 and Magical Mending as the cancel spell, plus Tempest Shield and Enfeeble.

body.text: **Raid spells and perks** are the **Magic, Attack and Artisan unlocks** the route casts on top of Agility: **Surge** for long dodges, the ***Death From Above!*** **Jump Attack** with **Magical Mending** as the cancel spell for ***Dotxy's*** cancels, **Tempest Shield** as a panic button and **Enfeeble** for the Heart.
**Three of them are mandatory**: Surge, the Jump Attack and a targeted AoE cancel spell.
Which spells and perks matter?

rows: Dive cancel, infinite double jump, flight
The cast you cancel in the dive cancel

body.text: Values come from the wiki spell pages, cited below.
Which runes do you need?

rows: Windstep, Phase Dash, Tempest Shield, Superheat

body.text: **Law runes carry a source conflict.** The wiki states *"Law runes can be crafted at a rune altar at level 50 Runecrafting or higher"* ([Law Rune, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Law_Rune)); the Raid Lab Hardcore route lists Runecrafting 16. **Check the altar in-game.** **Garou Packs** drop **5 to 10 Law runes** at a **10/100** rate ([Garou Pack, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Garou_Pack)), which keeps Surge stocked while you level.
**Rune totals per run are a count you make yourself.** Count your casts in one clean practice run and stock double that.
What does Surge do?

**Surge** is a Magic spell that gives **three long dodges of 8 metres** each, with the charges lasting **two minutes** ([Surge, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Surge)). ***SamFPlays*** built the **Phase Dash and Surge combo** on it: *"click that like whatever your dash button is to activate surge. At the end when your momentum starts to die, jump and then double dash."* ([Every Skip Explained, 0:58](https://youtu.be/ESrrkdxD1fo?t=58)).

Since 1.0 you **cast Surge while moving**: *"you can now move while casting a range of spells, including Enchant Weapon, Windstep and Surge"* ([1.0 notes, Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1843481262704158)).
What is the Jump Attack?

**The Jump Attack** is the **plunging melee attack** unlocked by the Attack perk ***Death From Above!*** at **Attack 25** ([Death From Above!, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Death_From_Above!)). Jagex describes the trigger in 1.0.1: *"above the max height of the double jump's arc from the ground, inputting an attack will plunge you downward to slam into unfortunate victims below... And yes, Windstep counts here."* ([1.0.1 notes, Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1374490/view/1846651706673783)).

**Hold a melee weapon with a plunge animation.** ***Nanobit*** warns: *"remember that DScim doesn't have a plunge animation, so you need something else equipped"* ([7:01, 5:07](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=307)). Jagex's 1.0.1.2 notes *"Fixed an issue where the Dragon Scimitar would not allow users to Jump Attack in certain circumstances"*, so **test the Dragon Scimitar's plunge in-game** before you carry it as your only melee weapon.
Why is Magical Mending the cancel spell?

**The cancel spell** is the targeted AoE cast that ***Dotxy's*** **dive cancel** interrupts: *"instantly exit the jump attack animation and ending lag by casting a targeted AOE spell, cancel the cast to gain full movement over your character instantly"* ([Dive Cancel, description](https://youtu.be/LGCddmk_TnM?t=0)). Any targeted AoE spell works, and the community default is **Magical Mending**. ***FastTipsGaming***: *"Everyone pretty much agrees that magical mending is the best one to use because most people unlock it earlier than the others."* ([Infinite Jump, 0:17](https://youtu.be/U0_KPXu28qw?t=17)).

**Superheat** at **Artisan 20** is the lower option, and it sits on ***Dotxy's*** own ring in his flight video ([Sanctum flight, 0:07](https://youtu.be/GeWbo4GpFEg?t=7)). Whether a cancelled cast spends runes or starts the cooldown is a **test step**: cast-and-cancel ten times and watch your rune count.
Which ring slots do the runners use?

***Nanobit***: *"I'm using Q1E for the plunge-cancel tech, and Q7 a lot of the time to windstep."* ([reply on the 7:01](https://youtu.be/doVQ9Ph256g?t=0)). Full keybinds are in the [setup checklist](#/kb?p=post%3Araid-speedrun-setup-checklist).
What do Tempest Shield and Enfeeble add?

**Tempest Shield** *"prevents all damage while blocking, including normally unblockable attacks"* for **15 Air runes** at **Attack 11** ([Tempest Shield, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Tempest_Shield)). It is the **safety option** on the hardcore-safe build.

**Enfeeble** at **Magic 61** weakens the target's attacks; the wiki page is a stub with no effect size ([Enfeeble, wiki](https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki/w/Enfeeble)). The Raid Lab requirement list attaches it to the **Heart phase**.
When do you unlock each one?

On the Raid Lab Hardcore route, **Tempest Shield**, **Surge** and **Superheat** arrive in **Phase 2** (Ghornfell, the level-11 power spike). **Magical Mending** arrives in **Phase 3** (Fellhollow). *Death From Above!* lands between Attack 11 and Attack 30, in **Phase 4**. **Enfeeble** arrives in **Phase 5** (Umbral Sands).
What this means when you run

items: **Unlock Death From Above!** at Attack 25 and carry a melee weapon with a plunge animation.
**Put Magical Mending on slot 1** and Windstep on slot 7, the way ***Nanobit*** does.
**Stock Astral and Law runes** for Surge, from the altar or from Garou Packs.
